papers.title: Barriers to Viral Hepatitis Elimination and New Strategies to Overcome Them in Low- and Middle-Income Countries.
papers.abstract: Chronic infections with hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), and hepatitis D virus (HDV) are major causes of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) worldwide. The greatest burden is borne by low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Despite the availability of highly effective preventive tools, simplified diagnostics, and affordable antiviral therapies, progress toward the World Health Organization's (WHO) goal of eliminating viral hepatitis as a public health threat by 2030 is insufficient in most LMICs. Gaps persist throughout the entire care continuum, from vaccination and the prevention of mother-to-child transmission to screening, confirmatory testing, linkage to care, treatment initiation, and long-term follow-up. Structural weaknesses in health systems, limited laboratory infrastructure, centralised models of care, financial constraints, stigma, and fragmented disease-specific programmes continue to hinder large-scale implementation. This article examines the main barriers encountered across the viral hepatitis care cascade, from prevention and testing to treatment and long-term follow-up. It discusses practical approaches to overcoming them, including simplified diagnostic and treatment pathways, point-of-care and near-point-of-care technologies, self-testing, integrated testing platforms, decentralised care, and task sharing. Attention is given to the prevention of mother-to-child transmission, the needs of populations underserved by conventional healthcare systems, and comorbidities that influence liver disease progression. In conclusion, technological advances alone will not be sufficient. Progress will also depend on stronger health systems, decentralised models of care, and the integration of viral hepatitis services into existing healthcare programmes.

papers.title_zh: 低收入和中等收入国家消除病毒性肝炎的障碍以及克服这些障碍的新策略。
papers.source_body_en: Chronic infections with hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), and hepatitis D virus (HDV) are major causes of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) worldwide. The greatest burden is borne by low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Despite the availability of highly effective preventive tools, simplified diagnostics, and affordable antiviral therapies, progress toward the World Health Organization's (WHO) goal of eliminating viral hepatitis as a public health threat by 2030 is insufficient in most LMICs. Gaps persist throughout the entire care continuum, from vaccination and the prevention of mother-to-child transmission to screening, confirmatory testing, linkage to care, treatment initiation, and long-term follow-up. Structural weaknesses in health systems, limited laboratory infrastructure, centralised models of care, financial constraints, stigma, and fragmented disease-specific programmes continue to hinder large-scale implementation. This article examines the main barriers encountered across the viral hepatitis care cascade, from prevention and testing to treatment and long-term follow-up. It discusses practical approaches to overcoming them, including simplified diagnostic and treatment pathways, point-of-care and near-point-of-care technologies, self-testing, integrated testing platforms, decentralised care, and task sharing. Attention is given to the prevention of mother-to-child transmission, the needs of populations underserved by conventional healthcare systems, and comorbidities that influence liver disease progression. In conclusion, technological advances alone will not be sufficient. Progress will also depend on stronger health systems, decentralised models of care, and the integration of viral hepatitis services into existing healthcare programmes.

papers.title: Application of the Information-Knowledge-Attitude-Practice Model in Breastfeeding Management for Pregnant Women with High Hepatitis B Virus Load.
papers.abstract: Ping Yang,1,* Si Chen,2,* Qiuyun Li,1 Yuzhen Zhang,1 Changjie Li,1 Wenjuan Xu,1 Haihua Yu,1 Lili Zhang21Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, Beijing You’an Hospital, Affiliated to Capital Medical University, Beijing, 100069, People’s Republic of China; 2Beijing You’an Hospital, Affiliated to Capital Medical University, Beijing, 100069, People’s Republic of China*These authors contributed equally to this workCorrespondence: Lili Zhang, Beijing You’an Hospital, Affiliated to Capital Medical University, No. 8, Xizhoutiao, You’anmenwai, Fengtai District, Beijing, 100069, People’s Republic of China, Tel +86 13716162977, Email zhanglyliy@163.comObjective: This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of the Information–Knowledge–Attitude–Practice (IKAP) model in breastfeeding management for pregnant women with high hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA loads (≥ 2 × 105 IU/mL).Methods: A prospective quasi-experimental study enrolled 136 eligible women between January 2023 and October 2023. Based on compliance, 68 who received the full IKAP-based intervention were assigned to the experimental group, and 68 who received routine health education served as controls. The experimental group received systematic, individualised IKAP-model education from the second trimester through 12 months postpartum, progressing through information, knowledge, attitude and practice stages. The control group received routine education (eg, prenatal classes, outpatient consultations). Primary outcomes (exclusive breastfeeding rate and self-efficacy at 42 days postpartum) and neonatal HBV transmission blockade outcomes at 7– 8 months were compared.Results: The exclusive breastfeeding rate at 42 days was significantly higher in the intervention group (85.29%) than in the control group (67.65%) (absolute risk difference = 17.64%, relative risk = 1.26, p 0.05).Conclusion: The phased IKAP model demonstrated superior outcomes compared with conventional education, safely increasing exclusive breastfeeding rates by approximately 17% and enhancing feeding confidence in high-risk mothers. Despite limitations, such as a non-randomised, single-centre design, it provides an effective and scalable framework for real-world application in supporting this special population.Keywords: Hepatitis B virus, viral load, breastfeeding, patient education as topic

source_records.abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of the Information-Knowledge-Attitude-Practice (IKAP) model in breastfeeding management for pregnant women with high hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA loads (≥2 × 105 IU/mL). METHODS: A prospective quasi-experimental study enrolled 136 eligible women between January 2023 and October 2023. Based on compliance, 68 who received the full IKAP-based intervention were assigned to the experimental group, and 68 who received routine health education served as controls. The experimental group received systematic, individualised IKAP-model education from the second trimester through 12 months postpartum, progressing through information, knowledge, attitude and practice stages. The control group received routine education (eg, prenatal classes, outpatient consultations). Primary outcomes (exclusive breastfeeding rate and self-efficacy at 42 days postpartum) and neonatal HBV transmission blockade outcomes at 7-8 months were compared. RESULTS: The exclusive breastfeeding rate at 42 days was significantly higher in the intervention group (85.29%) than in the control group (67.65%) (absolute risk difference = 17.64%, relative risk = 1.26, p 0.05). CONCLUSION: The phased IKAP model demonstrated superior outcomes compared with conventional education, safely increasing exclusive breastfeeding rates by approximately 17% and enhancing feeding confidence in high-risk mothers. Despite limitations, such as a non-randomised, single-centre design, it provides an effective and scalable framework for real-world application in supporting this special population.

elements_en.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of the Information–Knowledge–Attitude–Practice (IKAP) model in breastfeeding management for pregnant women with high hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA loads (≥ 2 × 105 IU/mL).
elements_en.study_design_and_population: A prospective quasi-experimental study enrolled 136 eligible women between January 2023 and October 2023. Based on compliance, 68 who received the full IKAP-based intervention were assigned to the experimental group, and 68 who received routine health education served as controls.
elements_en.methods: The experimental group received systematic, individualised IKAP-model education from the second trimester through 12 months postpartum, progressing through information, knowledge, attitude and practice stages. The control group received routine education (eg, prenatal classes, outpatient consultations).
elements_en.main_results: The exclusive breastfeeding rate at 42 days was significantly higher in the intervention group (85.29%) than in the control group (67.65%) (absolute risk difference = 17.64%, relative risk = 1.26, p 0.05).
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The phased IKAP model demonstrated superior outcomes compared with conventional education, safely increasing exclusive breastfeeding rates by approximately 17% and enhancing feeding confidence in high-risk mothers.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide an effective and scalable framework for real-world application in supporting pregnant women with high hepatitis B virus loads.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Despite limitations, such as a non-randomised, single-centre design, it provides an effective and scalable framework for real-world application in supporting this special population.

papers.title: Serum Interleukin-6 Concentrations in Patients with Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C Virus Infections: A Comparative Cross-sectional Study
papers.abstract: Background: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) infections are major causes of chronic liver disease and are associated with complex host immune and inflammatory responses. Interleukin-6 (IL-6) is an important pro-inflammatory cytokine involved in immune regulation and hepatic inflammation. However, differences in circulating IL-6 levels between HBV and HCV infections remain of interest. Objective: This study aimed to compare serum IL-6 concentrations between patients with HBV and HCV infections. Methods: A comparative cross-sectional study was conducted among 38 patients with viral hepatitis, including 7 patients with HBV infection and 31 patients with HCV infection. Serum IL-6 concentrations were measured using a commercially available ELISA kit (Melsin Medical Co., China) and expressed in pg/mL. IL-6 levels were compared between the two groups using an appropriate independent-group statistical test. Statistical significance was set at P < 0.05. Results: The mean serum IL-6 concentration was higher in patients with HBV infection than in those with HCV infection (13.95 ± 8.07 vs. 10.87 ± 4.03 pg/mL, respectively). The mean difference between the HCV and HBV groups was −3.08 pg/mL (95% CI: −9.37 to 3.21). However, the difference was not statistically significant (Welch's t-test, P = 0.297). The standardised effect size was moderate (Cohen's d = −0.59). Conclusion: Patients with HBV infection demonstrated a higher mean serum IL-6 concentration than patients with HCV infection in the studied population; however, this difference was not statistically significant. These findings do not provide sufficient evidence of a differential serum IL-6 response between HBV and HCV infections in this study. Further studies with larger sample sizes and additional clinical, biochemical, and virological parameters are warranted to clarify the inflammatory cytokine profiles associated with HBV and HCV infections.
papers.journal: International Research Journal of Gastroenterology and Hepatology

papers.title_zh: 乙型肝炎病毒和丙型肝炎病毒感染患者血清白细胞介素-6浓度的比较横断面研究
papers.source_body_en: Background: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) infections are major causes of chronic liver disease and are associated with complex host immune and inflammatory responses. Interleukin-6 (IL-6) is an important pro-inflammatory cytokine involved in immune regulation and hepatic inflammation. However, differences in circulating IL-6 levels between HBV and HCV infections remain of interest. Objective: This study aimed to compare serum IL-6 concentrations between patients with HBV and HCV infections. Methods: A comparative cross-sectional study was conducted among 38 patients with viral hepatitis, including 7 patients with HBV infection and 31 patients with HCV infection. Serum IL-6 concentrations were measured using a commercially available ELISA kit (Melsin Medical Co., China) and expressed in pg/mL. IL-6 levels were compared between the two groups using an appropriate independent-group statistical test. Statistical significance was set at P < 0.05. Results: The mean serum IL-6 concentration was higher in patients with HBV infection than in those with HCV infection (13.95 ± 8.07 vs. 10.87 ± 4.03 pg/mL, respectively). The mean difference between the HCV and HBV groups was −3.08 pg/mL (95% CI: −9.37 to 3.21). However, the difference was not statistically significant (Welch's t-test, P = 0.297). The standardised effect size was moderate (Cohen's d = −0.59). Conclusion: Patients with HBV infection demonstrated a higher mean serum IL-6 concentration than patients with HCV infection in the studied population; however, this difference was not statistically significant. These findings do not provide sufficient evidence of a differential serum IL-6 response between HBV and HCV infections in this study. Further studies with larger sample sizes and additional clinical, biochemical, and virological parameters are warranted to clarify the inflammatory cytokine profiles associated with HBV and HCV infections.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)和丙型肝炎病毒(HCV)感染是慢性肝病的主要病因,并与复杂的免疫和炎症反应相关。白细胞介素-6(IL-6)是一种重要的促炎细胞因子,参与免疫调节和肝脏炎症。然而,HBV和HCV感染之间循环IL-6水平的差异仍值得关注。目的:本研究旨在比较HBV和HCV感染患者的血清IL-6浓度。方法:在38名病毒性肝炎患者中进行了一项比较横断面研究,包括7名HBV感染患者和31名HCV感染患者。使用市售的ELISA试剂盒(Melsin Medical Co.,中国)测量血清IL-6浓度,并以pg/mL表示。采用适当的独立组统计检验方法比较两组之间的IL-6水平。统计学显著性设定为P < 0.05。结果:HBV感染患者的平均血清IL-6浓度高于HCV感染患者(分别为13.95 ± 8.07 pg/mL和10.87 ± 4.03 pg/mL)。HCV组与HBV组之间的平均差异为−3.08 pg/mL(95% CI:−9.37至3.21)。然而,该差异在统计学上并不显著(Welch's t-test,P = 0.297)。标准化效应量为中等(Cohen's d = −0.59)。结论:在本研究人群中,HBV感染患者的平均血清IL-6浓度高于HCV感染患者;然而,这种差异在统计学上并不显著。这些发现不足以证明HBV和HCV感染之间存在差异的血清IL-6反应。需要进一步进行更大样本量的研究,并纳入更多的临床、生化和病毒学参数,以明确与HBV和HCV感染相关的炎症细胞因子谱。

papers.title: Adult hepatitis B vaccination coverage and infection prevalence in Lagos, Nigeria: findings from a facility-based world hepatitis day study
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is a vaccine-preventable disease, and the Global Health Sector Strategy on Viral Hepatitis aims to eliminate viral hepatitis as a public health threat by 2030. Vaccination is prioritized as a key intervention for achieving this goal. The Nigerian Institute of Medical Research (NIMR) conducts annual World Hepatitis Day campaigns to increase awareness and promote HBV prevention in line with global elimination efforts. This study assessed the impact and uptake of an HBV vaccination programme implemented at NIMR and identified strategies to improve adult vaccination uptake in Nigeria. Method A free HBV screening and vaccination programme was conducted for community members between 28 July 2015 and February 2016 as part of the World Hepatitis Day campaign. Participants were screened for hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) using the SD Bioline HBsAg Rapid Test kit. Individuals who tested positive were referred for further clinical evaluation, while those who tested negative were enrolled for vaccination using a three-dose schedule at 0, 1, and 6 months. Demographic characteristics and travel distance to NIMR were collected and analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics, and variables significant at the bivariate level were entered into multivariate logistic regression. Result Over the 10-year study period (2015–2025), the overall HBsAg prevalence was 9.21% among 2,824 individuals tested. In the baseline 2015 cohort, 553 participants were screened, revealing a 9.0% ( n = 50) positivity rate and leaving 503 individuals eligible for immunization. Of these, 402 (80.0%) consented to participate and received the first vaccine dose. While Dose 2 completion was high at 85.6%, final Dose 3 completion dropped to 67.4% among tracked participants ( n = 344), representing 57.7% of the total enrolled cohort and yielding a 42.3% loss to follow-up rate. Notably, living near the vaccination center was significantly associated with lower odds of series completion. Conclusion HBsAg prevalence was high, while vaccination completion was suboptimal. Residential distance from the vaccination centre was associated with vaccine-series completion, although additional factors likely contributed to loss to follow-up. Decentralized mobile clinics and shorter vaccination schedules could reduce loss to follow-up and strengthen adult HBV immunization in Nigeria.

papers.title_zh: 尼日利亚拉各斯成人乙型肝炎 疫苗接种 覆盖率和感染 患病率:基于设施的世界肝炎日研究的结果
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is a vaccine-preventable disease, and the Global Health Sector Strategy on Viral Hepatitis aims to eliminate viral hepatitis as a public health threat by 2030. Vaccination is prioritized as a key intervention for achieving this goal. The Nigerian Institute of Medical Research (NIMR) conducts annual World Hepatitis Day campaigns to increase awareness and promote HBV prevention in line with global elimination efforts. This study assessed the impact and uptake of an HBV vaccination programme implemented at NIMR and identified strategies to improve adult vaccination uptake in Nigeria. Method A free HBV screening and vaccination programme was conducted for community members between 28 July 2015 and February 2016 as part of the World Hepatitis Day campaign. Participants were screened for hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) using the SD Bioline HBsAg Rapid Test kit. Individuals who tested positive were referred for further clinical evaluation, while those who tested negative were enrolled for vaccination using a three-dose schedule at 0, 1, and 6 months. Demographic characteristics and travel distance to NIMR were collected and analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics, and variables significant at the bivariate level were entered into multivariate logistic regression. Result Over the 10-year study period (2015–2025), the overall HBsAg prevalence was 9.21% among 2,824 individuals tested. In the baseline 2015 cohort, 553 participants were screened, revealing a 9.0% ( n = 50) positivity rate and leaving 503 individuals eligible for immunization. Of these, 402 (80.0%) consented to participate and received the first vaccine dose. While Dose 2 completion was high at 85.6%, final Dose 3 completion dropped to 67.4% among tracked participants ( n = 344), representing 57.7% of the total enrolled cohort and yielding a 42.3% loss to follow-up rate. Notably, living near the vaccination center was significantly associated with lower odds of series completion. Conclusion HBsAg prevalence was high, while vaccination completion was suboptimal. Residential distance from the vaccination centre was associated with vaccine-series completion, although additional factors likely contributed to loss to follow-up. Decentralized mobile clinics and shorter vaccination schedules could reduce loss to follow-up and strengthen adult HBV immunization in Nigeria.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 感染是一种 疫苗 可预防疾病,全球卫生部门病毒性肝炎战略旨在到 2030 年消除病毒性肝炎这一公共卫生威胁。疫苗接种 被优先作为实现这一目标的关键干预措施。尼日利亚医学研究所 (NIMR) 每年都会举办世界肝炎日活动,以提高人们的认识并促进乙型肝炎的预防,以配合全球消除乙型肝炎的努力。本研究评估了 NIMR 实施的 HBV 疫苗接种 计划的影响和采用率,并确定了提高尼日利亚成人 疫苗接种 吸收率的策略。方法 作为世界肝炎日活动的一部分,2015 年 7 月 28 日至 2016 年 2 月期间,对社区成员进行了免费 HBV 筛查和 疫苗接种 计划。使用 SD Bioline HBsAg 快速检测试剂盒对参与者进行乙型肝炎表面抗原 (HBsAg) 筛查。检测呈阳性的个体被转介进行进一步的临床评估,而检测呈阴性的个体则在 0、1 和 6 个月时使用三剂方案登记参加 疫苗接种。使用描述性和推论性统计来收集和分析人口统计特征和到 NIMR 的旅行距离,并将双变量水平上显着的变量输入到多元逻辑回归中。结果 在 10 年研究期间(2015 年至 2025 年),2,824 名接受测试的个体中 HBsAg 患病率 的总体率为 9.21%。在 2015 年 队列研究 基线中,对 553 名参与者进行了筛查,结果显示阳性率为 9.0% (n = 50),其中 503 人符合免疫接种资格。其中,402 人 (80.0%) 同意参与并接受了第一剂 疫苗 剂量。虽然第 2 剂完成率高达 85.6%,但跟踪参与者 (n = 344) 中最终第 3 剂完成率下降至 67.4%,占 队列研究 登记总数的 57.7%,随访率损失 42.3%。值得注意的是,居住在 疫苗接种 中心附近与系列完成几率较低显着相关。结论 HBsAg 患病率 较高,而 疫苗接种 完成度欠佳。距 疫苗接种 中心的居住距离与 疫苗 系列的完成相关,尽管其他因素可能导致随访失败。分散的流动诊所和较短的 疫苗接种 时间表可以减少随访损失并加强尼日利亚成人乙肝疫苗接种。

papers.title: Cytokine signature behind occult hepatitis B virus infection
papers.abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is a serious public health threat and one of the leading causes of acute, chronic and occult hepatitis (OBI). Standard diagnostics that detect HBsAg are insufficient for identifying OBI, defined by the presence of hepatic DNA in the absence of detectable serum HBsAg. Accumulating evidence indicate that the inadequate immune responses are responsible for HBV persistency. Cytokines are known to be important chemical mediators that regulate the differentiation, proliferation and function of immune cells. The goal of this study is to investigate the cytokine signature in OBI patients. The study initially enrolled 6,773 healthy volunteers, after excluding individuals under 18 years of age, hepatitis B marker testing revealed 57 cases of OBI. As controls, 37 healthy donors with the absence of viral hepatitis markers, HIV, and somatic diseases were selected from the same initial cohort. Immune mediators (cytokines, chemokines, and growth factors) in blood plasma were measured with the MAGPIX multiplex analysis. We found high levels IL-10 and growth factors (EGF, FLT-3 L, TGFα, G-CSF, M-CSF, VEGF) in OBI patients. ROC analysis indicates that M-CSF, FLT-3 L, G-CSF, EGF, and TGFα possess diagnostic potential as biomarkers for OBI. Based on the results of decision tree, we established that combined detection of M-CSF and FLT-3 L is more valuable in terms OBI diagnostic. OBI is characterized by a dominant anti-inflammatory and pro-fibrotic background, mediated by cytokines such as IL-10 and TGF-α, which facilitates viral persistence and promotes liver fibrosis despite the concurrent elevation of some pro-inflammatory signals. The activation of growth factors like TGF-α and EGF drives aberrant tissue repair, resulting in incomplete regeneration and scarring. The role of FLT-3 L appear dual, mediating hepatoprotection while simultaneously contributing to fibrotic progression. ROC and decision tree analysis indicates that several cytokines hold diagnostic potential as biomarkers for OBI.

source_records.title: Cytokine signature behind occult hepatitis B virus infection
source_records.abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is a serious public health threat and one of the leading causes of acute, chronic and occult hepatitis (OBI). Standard diagnostics that detect HBsAg are insufficient for identifying OBI, defined by the presence of hepatic DNA in the absence of detectable serum HBsAg. Accumulating evidence indicate that the inadequate immune responses are responsible for HBV persistency. Cytokines are known to be important chemical mediators that regulate the differentiation, proliferation and function of immune cells. The goal of this study is to investigate the cytokine signature in OBI patients. The study initially enrolled 6,773 healthy volunteers, after excluding individuals under 18 years of age, hepatitis B marker testing revealed 57 cases of OBI. As controls, 37 healthy donors with the absence of viral hepatitis markers, HIV, and somatic diseases were selected from the same initial cohort. Immune mediators (cytokines, chemokines, and growth factors) in blood plasma were measured with the MAGPIX multiplex analysis. We found high levels IL-10 and growth factors (EGF, FLT-3 L, TGFα, G-CSF, M-CSF, VEGF) in OBI patients. ROC analysis indicates that M-CSF, FLT-3 L, G-CSF, EGF, and TGFα possess diagnostic potential as biomarkers for OBI. Based on the results of decision tree, we established that combined detection of M-CSF and FLT-3 L is more valuable in terms OBI diagnostic. OBI is characterized by a dominant anti-inflammatory and pro-fibrotic background, mediated by cytokines such as IL-10 and TGF-α, which facilitates viral persistence and promotes liver fibrosis despite the concurrent elevation of some pro-inflammatory signals. The activation of growth factors like TGF-α and EGF drives aberrant tissue repair, resulting in incomplete regeneration and scarring. The role of FLT-3 L appear dual, mediating hepatoprotection while simultaneously contributing to fibrotic progression. ROC and decision tree analysis indicates that several cytokines hold diagnostic potential as biomarkers for OBI.

papers.abstract_zh: 乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)感染是一种严重的公共卫生威胁,是急性、慢性和隐匿性乙型肝炎(OBI)的主要原因之一。检测HBsAg的标准诊断方法不足以识别OBI,OBI定义为存在肝组织DNA但血清中无法检测到HBsAg的情况。越来越多的证据表明,不足的免疫应答会导致HBV持续存在。细胞因子是已知的重要化学介质,调节免疫细胞的分化、增殖和功能。本研究的目的是探讨OBI患者中的细胞因子特征。研究最初纳入了6,773名健康志愿者,在排除了18岁以下个体后,通过乙型肝炎标志物检测发现了57例OBI病例。作为对照组,从相同的初始队列研究中选取了37名无病毒性肝炎标志物、HIV和全身性疾病健康的供体。使用MAGPIX多重分析技术测量了血液浆液中的免疫介质(细胞因子、趋化因子和生长因子)。我们发现OBI患者中IL-10和生长因子(EGF、FLT-3 L、TGFα、G-CSF、M-CSF、VEGF)水平较高。ROC分析表明,M-CSF、FLT-3 L、G-CSF、EGF和TGFα具有作为OBI诊断生物标志物的潜力。基于决策树分析的结果,我们确定联合检测M-CSF和FLT-3 L在OBI诊断中更具价值。OBI的特点是具有占主导地位的抗炎和促纤维化背景,由IL-10和TGF-α等细胞因子介导,这有助于病毒持续存在,并在一些促炎信号同时升高时促进肝纤维化。TGF-α和EGF等生长因子的激活会驱动异常的组织修复,导致再生不全和瘢痕形成。FLT-3 L的作用似乎具有双重性,一方面介导肝保护,另一方面同时促进纤维化进程。ROC和决策树分析表明,几种细胞因子具有作为OBI诊断生物标志物的潜力。

papers.title: A Ganoderma lucidum Polysaccharide-Modified Nanoadjuvant Elicits Potent Cellular Immunity for Hepatitis B Vaccine
papers.abstract: Background: Aluminum-adjuvanted hepatitis B vaccines effectively prevent primary HBV infection but predominantly favor humoral immunity and have limited capacity to induce strong cellular responses. To improve immune-response quality, we developed a Ganoderma lucidum polysaccharide-modified hybrid nanoparticle adjuvant (GHNP) for hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) vaccination. Methods: Cationic PEG-PCL/DOTAP hybrid nanoparticles (HNPs) were surface-modified with Ganoderma lucidum polysaccharide (GLP) at different mass ratios and characterized by particle size, polydispersity index, zeta potential, and transmission electron microscopy. Antigen uptake, RAW264.7 cell viability, MHC II expression, and TLR2/4-associated TNF-α secretion were evaluated in vitro. C57BL/6 mice were immunized intramuscularly with PBS, HBsAg, HBsAg + Aluminum, HBsAg@HNP, or HBsAg@GHNP6 on Days 0, 14, and 28. HBsAg-specific antibodies, splenocyte activation, proliferation, and cytokine secretion were assessed. Results: GHNP6 showed suitable physicochemical properties, acceptable cytocompatibility at concentrations up to 10 μg·mL−1, and efficient model-antigen uptake. GHNP increased MHC II expression in RAW264.7 cells, and TLR2/4 inhibition reduced nanoparticle-associated TNF-α secretion, supporting involvement of these pathways in immune activation. In vivo, HBsAg@GHNP6 induced robust HBsAg-specific IgG responses and a higher IgG2a/IgG1 ratio than HBsAg@HNP and HBsAg + Aluminum. It also produced the highest splenocyte proliferation after HBsAg restimulation, with lower IL-6 secretion than HBsAg + Aluminum and moderately increased IFN-γ compared with PBS and free HBsAg. Conclusions: GHNP integrates nanoparticle-assisted antigen delivery with GLP-mediated immunomodulation and represents a promising strategy for enhancing cellular immune responses while maintaining humoral immunity in HBsAg vaccination.

To improve immune-response quality, we developed a Ganoderma lucidum polysaccharide-modified hybrid nanoparticle adjuvant (GHNP) for hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) vaccination. Methods: Cationic PEG-PCL/DOTAP hybrid nanoparticles (HNPs) were surface-modified with Ganoderma lucidum polysaccharide (GLP) at different mass ratios and characterized by particle size, polydispersity index, zeta potential, and transmission electron microscopy. Antigen uptake, RAW264.7 cell viability, MHC II expression, and TLR2/4-associated TNF-α secretion were evaluated in vitro. C57BL/6 mice were immunized intramuscularly with PBS, HBsAg, HBsAg + Aluminum, HBsAg@HNP, or HBsAg@GHNP6 on Days 0, 14, and 28. HBsAg-specific antibodies, splenocyte activation, proliferation, and cytokine secretion were assessed. Results: GHNP6 showed suitable physicochemical properties, acceptable cytocompatibility at concentrations up to 10 μg·mL−1, and efficient model-antigen uptake. GHNP increased MHC II expression in RAW264.7 cells, and TLR2/4 inhibition reduced nanoparticle-associated TNF-α secretion, supporting involvement of these pathways in immune activation. In vivo, HBsAg@GHNP6 induced robust HBsAg-specific IgG responses and a higher IgG2a/IgG1 ratio than HBsAg@HNP and HBsAg + Aluminum. It also produced the highest splenocyte proliferation after HBsAg restimulation, with lower IL-6 secretion than HBsAg + Aluminum and moderately increased IFN-γ compared with PBS and free HBsAg. Conclusions: GHNP integrates nanoparticle-assisted antigen delivery with GLP-mediated immunomodulation and represents a promising strategy for enhancing cellular immune responses while maintaining humoral immunity in HBsAg vaccination.

analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that GHNP could improve the quality of immune responses in hepatitis B vaccination, potentially leading to better protection against both acute and chronic HBV infections.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to improve the immune response of hepatitis B vaccines by developing a Ganoderma lucidum polysaccharide-modified hybrid nanoparticle adjuvant (GHNP). The researchers evaluated the physicochemical properties and immunomodulatory effects of GHNP in vitro and in vivo using C57BL/6 mice. Results showed that GHNP enhanced MHC II expression and induced robust HBsAg-specific IgG responses with a higher IgG2a/IgG1 ratio compared to other adjuvants. It also promoted splenocyte proliferation and increased IFN-γ secretion. The authors concluded that GHNP represents a promising strategy for enhancing cellular immunity while maintaining humoral immunity in HBV vaccination. However, the study is limited to experimental models, and the evidence is moderate.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 铝佐剂乙型肝炎 疫苗 可有效预防原发性 HBV 感染,但主要有利于体液免疫,并且诱导强烈细胞反应的能力有限。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: C57BL/6 小鼠在第 0、14 和 28 天用 PBS、HBsAg、HBsAg + 铝、HBsAg@HNP 或 HBsAg@GHNP6 进行肌内免疫。
elements_zh.methods: 采用不同质量比的灵芝多糖(GLP)对阳离子 PEG-PCL/DOTAP 杂化纳米颗粒(HNP)进行表面修饰,并通过粒径、多分散指数、zeta 电位和 传播 电镜进行表征。体外评估抗原摄取、RAW264.7 细胞活力、MHC II 表达和 TLR2/4 相关 TNF-α 分泌。评估了 HBsAg 特异性抗体、脾细胞活化、增殖和细胞因子分泌。
elements_zh.main_results: GHNP6 显示出合适的理化特性、浓度高达 10 μg·mL−1 时可接受的细胞相容性以及有效的模型抗原摄取。GHNP 增加 RAW264.7 细胞中的 MHC II 表达,TLR2/4 抑制减少纳米颗粒相关的 TNF-α 分泌,支持这些途径参与免疫激活。在体内,与 HBsAg@HNP 和 HBsAg + 铝相比,HBsAg@GHNP6 诱导了强大的 HBsAg 特异性 IgG 反应,并且 IgG2a/IgG1 比率更高。在 HBsAg 再刺激后,它还产生最高的脾细胞增殖,与 HBsAg + 铝相比,IL-6 分泌量较低,与 PBS 和游离 HBsAg 相比,IFN-γ 适度增加。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: GHNP 将纳米颗粒辅助抗原递送与 GLP 介导的免疫调节相结合,代表了一种增强细胞 免疫应答 同时维持 HBsAg 疫苗接种 体液免疫的有前途的策略。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,GHNP 可以提高乙型肝炎 免疫应答 的质量,从而可能更好地预防急性和慢性 HBV 感染。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于使用小鼠进行的体外和体内实验,可能无法完全代表人类免疫应答。证据是温和的,因为它是基于实验模型而不是临床试验。

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:铝佐剂乙型肝炎 疫苗 可有效预防原发性 HBV 感染,但主要有利于体液免疫,并且诱导强烈细胞反应的能力有限。为了提高免疫反应质量,我们开发了一种灵芝多糖修饰的乙型肝炎表面抗原(HBsAg)混合纳米颗粒佐剂(GHNP)疫苗接种。方法:采用不同质量比的灵芝多糖(GLP)对阳离子PEG-PCL/DOTAP杂化纳米粒子(HNPs)进行表面修饰,并通过粒径、多分散指数、zeta电位和传播电镜进行表征。体外评估抗原摄取、RAW264.7 细胞活力、MHC II 表达和 TLR2/4 相关 TNF-α 分泌。C57BL/6 小鼠在第 0、14 和 28 天用 PBS、HBsAg、HBsAg + 铝、HBsAg@HNP 或 HBsAg@GHNP6 进行肌内免疫。评估 HBsAg 特异性抗体、脾细胞活化、增殖和细胞因子分泌。结果:GHNP6 显示出合适的理化特性、浓度高达 10 μg·mL−1 时可接受的细胞相容性以及有效的模型抗原摄取。GHNP 增加 RAW264.7 细胞中的 MHC II 表达,TLR2/4 抑制减少纳米颗粒相关的 TNF-α 分泌,支持这些途径参与免疫激活。在体内,与 HBsAg@HNP 和 HBsAg + 铝相比,HBsAg@GHNP6 诱导了强大的 HBsAg 特异性 IgG 反应,并且 IgG2a/IgG1 比率更高。在 HBsAg 再刺激后,它还产生最高的脾细胞增殖,与 HBsAg + 铝相比,IL-6 分泌量较低,与 PBS 和游离 HBsAg 相比,IFN-γ 适度增加。结论:GHNP 将纳米颗粒辅助抗原递送与 GLP 介导的免疫调节相结合,代表了一种增强细胞 免疫应答 同时维持 HBsAg 疫苗接种 体液免疫的有前途的策略。

analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: GHNP 将纳米颗粒辅助抗原递送与 GLP 介导的免疫调节相结合,代表了一种增强细胞 免疫应答 同时维持 HBsAg 疫苗接种 体液免疫的有前途的策略。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,GHNP 可以提高乙型肝炎 免疫应答 的质量,从而可能更好地预防急性和慢性 HBV 感染。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于使用小鼠进行的体外和体内实验,可能无法完全代表人类免疫应答。证据是温和的,因为它是基于实验模型而不是临床试验。

papers.title: Biological interpretation of baseline hepatitis B surface antigen and cirrhosis in determining interferon treatment duration
papers.abstract: The recent identification of baseline hepatitis B surface antigen and cirrhosis as independent predictors of extended interferon therapy provides a valuable clinical framework, yet the biological mechanisms underlying these associations require further elucidation. In this opinion review, we interpret these factors not merely as statistical covariates but as pathological surrogates for the virus-host equilibrium. We propose that high baseline hepatitis B surface antigen may reflect a deeply entrenched intrahepatic viral reservoir and may create an antigen-rich environment that impairs effective antiviral immunity. Concurrently, cirrhosis may be better understood as a spectrum of architectural remodeling in which vascular changes and sinusoidal defenestration could limit immune surveillance and affect local therapeutic access. Consequently, treatment durations exceeding 48 weeks may be required, at least in part, to overcome these profound immunological and structural barriers. We advocate shifting future predictive modeling from binary clinical definitions to a granular integration of viral kinetics and histological morphology to refine precision medicine in chronic hepatitis B.

papers.abstract_zh: 最近将基线乙型肝炎表面抗原和肝硬化确定为延长干扰素治疗的独立预测因子,提供了有价值的临床框架,但这些关联背后的生物学机制需要进一步阐明。在本意见综述中,我们不仅将这些因素解释为统计协变量,而且将其解释为病毒-宿主 平衡的病理替代物。我们认为,高基线乙型肝炎表面抗原可能反映了肝内根深蒂固的病毒 储存宿主,并可能创造一个富含抗原的环境,损害有效的 抗病毒药物 免疫力。同时,肝硬化可以更好地理解为一系列结构重塑,其中血管变化和肝窦开窗可能限制免疫 监测 并影响局部治疗途径。因此,可能需要(至少部分)超过 48 周的 治疗 持续时间来克服这些深刻的免疫学和结构障碍。我们主张将未来的预测模型从二元临床定义转变为病毒动力学和组织学形态的精细整合,以完善 慢性乙型肝炎 中的精准医学。

papers.title: Prevalence and associated risk factors of hepatitis B virus among Rohingya refugees: a hospital-based study at Cox’s Bazar, Bangladesh
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a critical public health challenge globally, with particular concern for vulnerable populations like Rohingya refugee or forcibly displaced Myanmar nationals (FDMNs) residing in Cox’s Bazar refugee camps. This cross-sectional study aimed to assess the prevalence of HBV among Rohingya refugees admitted to a tertiary care hospital. Methods This cross-sectional study conducted in the Department of Medicine, Cox’s Bazar Medical College Hospital from August 2018 to January 2019. A total of 384 hospital admitted Rohingya refugees were enrolled following informed written consent. Data collection was conducted through face-to-face interviews and laboratory analyses of blood samples for HBsAg. Collected data were analysed by the statistical software SPSS version 22. Results The mean age of study patients was 44.96 ± 15.62 (SD) years, with a slight female predominance (51.6% female vs. The frequency of positive HBsAg cases was 3.1%. Among the study population, the most common potential risk factors identified were body piercing (46.6%), tobacco consumption (40.4%), and injection drug use (40%). However, a statistical association of positive HBsAg cases was observed only with low monthly income (< 10,000 Bangladesh Tk) ( p <.05) and unsafe blood transfusions ( p <.05). Conclusion In this study, seropositivity for hepatitis B virus was observed in 3.1% that needs to be addressed and treated properly. Appropriate strategic measures are advised to prevent further transmission.

papers.title_zh: 患病率 与 Rohingya 流亡者中的 乙型肝炎病毒 相关风险因素:孟加拉国科克斯巴扎尔医院基于的研究
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a critical public health challenge globally, with particular concern for vulnerable populations like Rohingya refugee or forcibly displaced Myanmar nationals (FDMNs) residing in Cox’s Bazar refugee camps. This cross-sectional study aimed to assess the prevalence of HBV among Rohingya refugees admitted to a tertiary care hospital. Methods This cross-sectional study conducted in the Department of Medicine, Cox’s Bazar Medical College Hospital from August 2018 to January 2019. A total of 384 hospital admitted Rohingya refugees were enrolled following informed written consent. Data collection was conducted through face-to-face interviews and laboratory analyses of blood samples for HBsAg. Collected data were analysed by the statistical software SPSS version 22. Results The mean age of study patients was 44.96 ± 15.62 (SD) years, with a slight female predominance (51.6% female vs. The frequency of positive HBsAg cases was 3.1%. Among the study population, the most common potential risk factors identified were body piercing (46.6%), tobacco consumption (40.4%), and injection drug use (40%). However, a statistical association of positive HBsAg cases was observed only with low monthly income (< 10,000 Bangladesh Tk) ( p <.05) and unsafe blood transfusions ( p <.05). Conclusion In this study, seropositivity for hepatitis B virus was observed in 3.1% that needs to be addressed and treated properly. Appropriate strategic measures are advised to prevent further transmission.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 感染仍然是全球面临的一项重大公共卫生挑战,特别关注居住在考克斯巴扎尔难民营的罗兴亚难民或被迫流离失所的缅甸国民 (FDMN) 等弱势群体。这项横断面研究旨在评估三级甲等医院收治的罗辛亚难民中乙型肝炎病毒的 患病率。方法 这项横断面研究于 2018 年 8 月至 2019 年 1 月在考克斯巴扎尔医学院医院医学部进行。在知情书面同意后,共有 384 名医院收治的罗兴亚难民被纳入。数据收集是通过面对面访谈和血液样本 HBsAg 实验室分析进行的。收集的数据通过统计软件 SPSS 22 版进行分析。结果 研究患者的平均年龄为 44.96 ± 15.62 (SD) 岁,女性稍多(女性 51.6%,HBsAg 阳性病例频率为 3.1%)。在研究人群中,最常见的潜在危险因素是身体穿孔(46.6%)、烟草消费(40.4%)和注射毒品使用(40%)。然而,仅在低月收入 (< 10,000 孟加拉国 Tk) (p <.05) 和不安全输血 (p <.05) 的情况下观察到 HBsAg 病例的统计关联,在本研究中,观察到 3.1% 的 乙型肝炎病毒 血清阳性,需要采取适当的战略措施来预防进一步的 传播。

papers.title: From mechanisms to practice: risk management and multidisciplinary decision-making for systemic treatment-related liver injury in HBV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a leading cause of cancer-related death globally, with chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection as the predominant risk factor. Systemic therapies including tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs), immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), and ICI-antiangiogenic combinations have revolutionized advanced HCC treatment. However, treatment-induced liver injury is a major concern, especially in HBV-related HCC patients with pre-existing inflammation, fibrosis, and cirrhosis, which raises risks of treatment interruption, impaired efficacy, and acute liver failure. Liver injury arises from direct cytotoxicity, immune-mediated hepatitis, vascular damage, and HBV reactivation. This review summarizes the pathophysiological mechanisms of treatment-related liver injury in HBV-related HCC, analyzes the hepatotoxic profiles of tyrosine kinase inhibitors, immune checkpoint inhibitors, combination regimens and emerging agents, and proposes a structured clinical management framework including pretreatment risk assessment, prophylaxis, monitoring, differential diagnosis and severity-based interventions supported by multidisciplinary care. It aims to offer evidence-based guidance for clinicians to preserve liver function while safely administering effective antitumor therapy. The review also highlights key knowledge gaps and future research directions, including predictive biomarkers, personalized risk stratification and proactive safety evaluation of new drugs.

However, treatment-induced liver injury is a major concern, especially in HBV-related HCC patients with pre-existing inflammation, fibrosis, and cirrhosis, which raises risks of treatment interruption, impaired efficacy, and acute liver failure. Liver injury arises from direct cytotoxicity, immune-mediated hepatitis, vascular damage, and HBV reactivation. This review summarizes the pathophysiological mechanisms of treatment-related liver injury in HBV-related HCC, analyzes the hepatotoxic profiles of tyrosine kinase inhibitors, immune checkpoint inhibitors, combination regimens and emerging agents, and proposes a structured clinical management framework including pretreatment risk assessment, prophylaxis, monitoring, differential diagnosis and severity-based interventions supported by multidisciplinary care. It aims to offer evidence-based guidance for clinicians to preserve liver function while safely administering effective antitumor therapy. The review also highlights key knowledge gaps and future research directions, including predictive biomarkers, personalized risk stratification and proactive safety evaluation of new drugs.

papers.abstract_zh: 肝细胞癌(HCC)是全球癌症相关死亡的主要原因之一,其中慢性乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)感染是主要的危险因素。包括酪氨酸激酶抑制剂(TKIs)、免疫检查点抑制剂(ICIs)以及ICI-抗血管生成联合方案在内的系统性治疗已彻底改变了晚期HCC的治疗格局。然而,治疗诱导的肝损伤是主要关注点,尤其是在HBV相关HCC患者中,由于存在既往的炎症、纤维化和肝硬化,这会增加治疗中断、疗效受损以及急性肝衰竭的风险。肝损伤的产生机制包括直接细胞毒性、免疫介导的肝炎、血管损伤以及HBV再激活。本文综述了HBV相关HCC中治疗相关肝损伤的病理生理机制,分析了酪氨酸激酶抑制剂、免疫检查点抑制剂、联合方案及新兴药物的肝毒性特征,并提出了一个结构化的临床管理框架,包括治疗前风险评估、预防措施、监测、多学科协作支持的鉴别诊断和基于严重程度的干预措施。旨在为临床医生提供循证指导,以在安全地给予有效抗肿瘤治疗的同时保持肝功能。本文还强调了关键的知识空白和未来研究方向,包括预测性生物标志物、个性化风险分层以及新药的主动安全性评估。

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to explore the potential of sequential immune therapy following nucleos(t)ide analogue withdrawal in managing chronic hepatitis B, addressing the challenge of viral rebound and immune reconstitution.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted as a clinical trial involving patients with chronic hepatitis B who had previously undergone nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy. Participants were followed over time to assess the outcomes of sequential immune therapy.
analysis.methods: The study employed sequential immune therapy protocols, including the use of interferon and other immunomodulatory agents, following nucleos(t)ide analogue withdrawal. Outcomes were defined based on virological and immunological markers.
analysis.main_results: The study observed that sequential immune therapy significantly reduced viral load in some patients and improved immune responses, although not all participants achieved sustained virological suppression.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as evidence that sequential immune therapy may offer a viable strategy for managing chronic hepatitis B post-treatment, highlighting its potential as a novel approach.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings could inform future treatment strategies for chronic hepatitis B, particularly in managing viral rebound and enhancing immune responses post-antiviral therapy.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's results are based on a limited sample size and may not be generalizable to all patient populations, suggesting a moderate level of evidence for the effectiveness of sequential immune therapy.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the effectiveness of sequential immune therapy following nucleos(t)ide analogue withdrawal in managing chronic hepatitis B. The research aimed to address the issue of viral rebound and immune reconstitution after treatment cessation. The study involved a clinical trial with patients who had previously undergone nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy, and the methods included the use of interferon and immunomodulatory agents. Results showed that sequential immune therapy reduced viral load and improved immune responses in some patients, though not all achieved sustained suppression. The authors interpret these findings as evidence that sequential immune therapy may be a novel approach for managing chronic hepatitis B. The study's implications suggest potential applications in treatment strategies for post-antiviral management. However, the limited sample size and possible lack of generalizability indicate a moderate level of evidence for the observed outcomes.

papers.title: Prevalence and Distribution of Hepatitis B Virus in Patients with SARS-CoV-2: Exploring Co-infection Impacts on Clinical Outcomes and Immune Response
papers.abstract: Background: The COVID-19 pandemic shows that SARS-CoV-2 interacts with various comorbidities, including chronic viral infections. HBV may induce chronic liver disease and hepatocellular carcinoma, a global health concern. Objective: The objective of this study was to investigate the effects of infected people with Hepatitis B virus and SARS-CoV-2 along with co-infection, immune response and clinical outcomes. Methodology: A cross-sectional study was conducted in the Department of Criminal Evidence, College of Science, University of Hillah, Babylon Iraq. From March to August 2024. A 100 patients with proven SARS-CoV-2 infection and HBV prevalence, 100 patients with confirmed infection alone, and 50 healthy controls from both sexes aged 10-65. Laboratory and Immunological markers were measured in patient blood samples. Results: Age was the main demographic difference between the COVID and HBV and COVID-19 alone groups (55 ± 10 years vs. 50 ± 12 years), and both groups were older than the control group (45 ± 14 years). Both COVID-19 groups experienced higher hospitalization (60.0% to 70.0%), oxygen consumption (25.0% to 35.0%), and critical care unit hospitalizations (15.0% to 25.0%) than the control group (5.0%). COVID and HBV had a 15.0% death rate compared to 8.0% for COVID-19 alone or 0% with the control group. The COVID + HBV group had the lowest immune response, with poorer anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgG, IgM, and T-cell activity and a higher rate of breakthrough infections. Conclusion: HBV co-infection severely worsens COVID-19 findings. In the COVID + HBV group, hospitalizations, ICU admissions, longer hospital stays, and fatalities were higher. Their poorer immune responses and higher liver inflammation and dysfunction likely worsened their fate. Bangladesh Journal of Infectious Diseases, June 2026;13(1):251-261

analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study was conducted in the Department of Criminal Evidence, College of Science, University of Hillah, Babylon Iraq, involving 100 patients with proven SARS-CoV-2 and HBV co-infection, 100 patients with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection alone, and 50 healthy controls aged 10-65.
analysis.methods: Laboratory and immunological markers were measured in patient blood samples. The study spanned from March to August 2024.
analysis.main_results: The COVID + HBV group had a 15.0% death rate, compared to 8.0% for the COVID-19 alone group and 0% for the control group. Both COVID-19 groups experienced higher hospitalization, oxygen consumption, and critical care unit hospitalizations than the control group. The COVID + HBV group showed the lowest immune response, with poorer anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgG, IgM, and T-cell activity and a higher rate of breakthrough infections.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that HBV co-infection significantly worsens the clinical outcomes of SARS-CoV-2 infection, likely due to poorer immune responses and higher liver inflammation and dysfunction.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that HBV co-infection may be a critical factor in the severity of SARS-CoV-2 outcomes, highlighting the need for targeted surveillance and management strategies in co-infected populations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design and the specific setting in Babylon, Iraq, which may affect generalizability. The evidence is moderate due to the observational nature and potential confounding factors.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the effects of co-infection with Hepatitis B virus (HBV) and SARS-CoV-2 on clinical outcomes and immune response. Conducted in Babylon, Iraq, from March to August 2024, it compared 100 co-infected patients, 100 with SARS-CoV-2 alone, and 50 healthy controls. Results showed that the co-infected group had higher hospitalization rates, ICU admissions, and mortality compared to the other groups. They also exhibited lower immune responses and higher breakthrough infections. The authors concluded that HBV co-infection exacerbates the severity of SARS-CoV-2 outcomes, likely due to immune and liver dysfunction. The study's findings have implications for understanding co-infection dynamics and improving clinical management. However, the cross-sectional design and limited geographic scope may affect the generalizability of the results, resulting in moderate confidence in the evidence.

elements_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore the impacts of co-infection with Hepatitis B virus and SARS-CoV-2 on clinical outcomes and immune response. The background highlights the interaction between SARS-CoV-2 and chronic viral infections during the COVID-19 pandemic.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study was conducted in the Department of Criminal Evidence, College of Science, University of Hillah, Babylon Iraq, involving 100 patients with proven SARS-CoV-2 and HBV co-infection, 100 patients with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection alone, and 50 healthy controls aged 10-65.
elements_en.methods: Laboratory and immunological markers were measured in patient blood samples. The study spanned from March to August 2024.
elements_en.main_results: The COVID + HBV group had a 15.0% death rate, compared to 8.0% for the COVID-19 alone group and 0% for the control group. Both COVID-19 groups experienced higher hospitalization, oxygen consumption, and critical care unit hospitalizations than the control group. The COVID + HBV group showed the lowest immune response, with poorer anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgG, IgM, and T-cell activity and a higher rate of breakthrough infections.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that HBV co-infection significantly worsens the clinical outcomes of SARS-CoV-2 infection, likely due to poorer immune responses and higher liver inflammation and dysfunction.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that HBV co-infection may be a critical factor in the severity of SARS-CoV-2 outcomes, highlighting the need for targeted surveillance and management strategies in co-infected populations.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design and the specific setting in Babylon, Iraq, which may affect generalizability. The evidence is moderate due to the observational nature and potential confounding factors.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 研究问题与背景:本研究旨在探讨 乙型肝炎病毒 与 SARS-CoV-2 共感染对临床结局及 免疫应答 的影响。背景强调了 COVID-19 大流行期间 SARS-CoV-2 与慢性病毒感染之间的相互作用。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 研究设计与人群:在伊拉克巴比伦希拉大学科学学院刑事证据系开展了一项横断面研究,纳入 100 名经证实 SARS-CoV-2 与 HBV 共感染的患者、100 名仅感染 SARS-CoV-2 的患者,以及 50 名年龄 10-65 岁的健康对照。
elements_zh.methods: 方法:对患者血样测定实验室和免疫学指标。研究时间为 2024 年 3 月至 8 月。
elements_zh.main_results: 主要结果:COVID+HBV 组死亡率为 15.0%,高于仅 COVID-19 组的 8.0% 和对照组的 0%。两组 COVID-19 患者的住院率、吸氧率和重症监护室入住率均高于对照组。COVID+HBV 组的 免疫应答 最低,抗 SARS-CoV-2 IgG、IgM 及 T 细胞活性较差,突破性感染率更高。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 解释与新颖性:作者得出结论,HBV 共感染显著恶化 SARS-CoV-2 感染的临床结局,可能与 免疫应答 较差以及肝脏炎症和功能障碍加重有关。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 科学与公共卫生意义:研究结果提示 HBV 共感染可能是 SARS-CoV-2 病情严重程度的关键因素,强调在共感染人群中需要针对性的 监测 与管理策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 局限性与证据强度:本研究受横断面设计及伊拉克巴比伦特定环境的限制,可能影响结果的推广性。由于观察性性质和潜在混杂因素,证据强度为中等。

papers.title_zh: 患病率 与 SARS-CoV-2 患者中 乙型肝炎病毒 的分布:探索共感染对临床结局及 免疫应答 的影响
papers.source_body_en: Background: The COVID-19 pandemic shows that SARS-CoV-2 interacts with various comorbidities, including chronic viral infections. HBV may induce chronic liver disease and hepatocellular carcinoma, a global health concern. Objective: The objective of this study was to investigate the effects of infected people with Hepatitis B virus and SARS-CoV-2 along with co-infection, immune response and clinical outcomes. Methodology: A cross-sectional study was conducted in the Department of Criminal Evidence, College of Science, University of Hillah, Babylon Iraq. From March to August 2024. A 100 patients with proven SARS-CoV-2 infection and HBV prevalence, 100 patients with confirmed infection alone, and 50 healthy controls from both sexes aged 10-65. Laboratory and Immunological markers were measured in patient blood samples. Results: Age was the main demographic difference between the COVID and HBV and COVID-19 alone groups (55 ± 10 years vs. 50 ± 12 years), and both groups were older than the control group (45 ± 14 years). Both COVID-19 groups experienced higher hospitalization (60.0% to 70.0%), oxygen consumption (25.0% to 35.0%), and critical care unit hospitalizations (15.0% to 25.0%) than the control group (5.0%). COVID and HBV had a 15.0% death rate compared to 8.0% for COVID-19 alone or 0% with the control group. The COVID + HBV group had the lowest immune response, with poorer anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgG, IgM, and T-cell activity and a higher rate of breakthrough infections. Conclusion: HBV co-infection severely worsens COVID-19 findings. In the COVID + HBV group, hospitalizations, ICU admissions, longer hospital stays, and fatalities were higher. Their poorer immune responses and higher liver inflammation and dysfunction likely worsened their fate. Bangladesh Journal of Infectious Diseases, June 2026;13(1):251-261
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:COVID-19 大流行表明 SARS-CoV-2 与多种合并症相互作用,包括慢性病毒感染。HBV 可能导致慢性肝病和肝细胞癌,构成全球健康问题。目的:本研究旨在调查 乙型肝炎病毒 与 SARS-CoV-2 共感染者的影响,以及共感染、免疫应答 与临床结局的关系。方法学:在伊拉克巴比伦希拉大学科学学院刑事证据系开展了一项横断面研究,时间为 2024 年 3 月至 8 月。纳入 100 名经证实 SARS-CoV-2 感染且合并 HBV 患病率 的患者、100 名仅感染 SARS-CoV-2 的患者,以及 50 名年龄 10-65 岁、男女均衡的健康对照。对患者血样测定实验室和免疫学指标。结果:年龄是 COVID+HBV 组与仅 COVID-19 组之间的主要人口学差异(55 ± 10 岁 vs. 50 ± 12 岁),且两组均年龄高于对照组(45 ± 14 岁)。两组 COVID-19 患者的住院率(60.0%~70.0%)、吸氧率(25.0%~35.0%)和重症监护室入住率(15.0%~25.0%)均高于对照组(5.0%)。COVID+HBV 组死亡率为 15.0%,高于仅 COVID-19 组的 8.0% 和对照组的 0%。COVID+HBV 组的 免疫应答 最低,抗 SARS-CoV-2 IgG、IgM 及 T 细胞活性较差,突破性感染率更高。结论:HBV 共感染显著加重 COVID-19 病情。COVID+HBV 组的住院率、ICU 收治率、住院时长及死亡率均更高。其 免疫应答 较差且肝脏炎症和功能障碍更严重,可能导致更差的预后。Bangladesh Journal of Infectious Diseases,June 2026;13(1):251-261

Search Search Home News One Step Closer to Elimination: PAHO Supports Trinidad and Tobago in Eliminating Mother to Child Transmission of HIV, Syphilis and Hepatitis B One Step Closer to Elimination: PAHO Supports Trinidad and Tobago in Eliminating Mother to Child Transmission of HIV, Syphilis and Hepatitis B Port-of-Spain, 7 September 2026 (PAHO): – Every mother hopes to give her child the healthiest possible start in life. Achieving that goal depends on more than medical care during delivery. It requires quality healthcare throughout pregnancy, reliable laboratory services, strong data systems and timely access to testing and treatment. In September 2026, the Ministry of Health, Trinidad and Tobago, with support from PAHO/WHO, completed a comprehensive national assessment of these critical services, marking an important milestone in the country's journey towards eliminating mother-to-child transmission of HIV, syphilis and hepatitis B. The assessment, conducted across multiple public and private health facilities, provided a critical opportunity to assess the systems, services and policies that protect mothers and newborns from preventable infections. More importantly, it established a clear roadmap for advancing Trinidad and Tobago's EMTCT certification process and strengthening services that benefit families across the country. The assessment mission also addressed a longstanding gap by examining how data, laboratory systems, clinical services and community engagement efforts work together to support disease elimination and achieve global targets. Over four days, multidisciplinary teams comprising representatives from the Ministry of Health, Regional Health Authorities, laboratory services, maternal and child health programmes, civil society organizations and PAHO/WHO visited antenatal clinics, maternity units, laboratories and private healthcare facilities throughout Trinidad and Tobago. The review followed the process through the healthcare system, examining every step from antenatal care and screening to treatment, delivery services and follow-up care for infants exposed to HIV, syphilis or hepatitis B. Teams also assessed laboratory quality assurance systems, surveillance mechanisms, referral pathways, data collection processes and community engagement frameworks. news.content_zh: 2026 年 9 月,特立尼达和多巴哥卫生部在泛美卫生组织/世界卫生组织的支持下完成了一项全面的国家评估,以评估其医疗保健系统为消除艾滋病毒、梅毒和乙型肝炎母婴 传播 的准备情况。该评估涉及多学科团队访问公共和私人医疗机构,包括西班牙港总医院、埃里克·威廉姆斯医学科学中心和特立尼达公共卫生实验室等主要机构。评估涵盖产前保健、实验室服务、监测机制和社区参与等关键领域。研究结果强调了改进的优势和机会,从而制定了一项国家行动计划,以推进 EMTCT 认证并加强疾病消除途径。该倡议以部长 Lackram Bodoe 博士于 2026 年 7 月发起的泛美卫生组织消除倡议为基础,旨在将预防新生儿感染的目标转变为可实现的现实。

Home/ Research Areas/ Infectious Disease & Vaccines News Brii Biosciences inches closer to functional cure for hepatitis B but future is uncertain New results from their Phase 2 trials show promise, but there could be issues moving to Phase 3. GSK's functional cure could be approved in the US before then. Written byAllison Whitten, PhD Aug 26, 2026| 3 min read Hepatitis B causes damage to the liver and affects hundreds of millions of people worldwide. Credit: iStock.com/SewcreamStudio Download PDF Register for free to listen to this article Listen with Speechify 0:00 3:00 The hepatitis B virus (HBV) vaccine is up to 90 percent effective at preventing HBV when given within 24 hours after birth. But for the hundreds of millions of people around the world who have already acquired the viral infection that attacks their liver, there is no cure. Current standard treatments consist of daily, lifelong antiviral therapies where the virus still hides within liver tissue. Therapies that lead to a functional cure for HBV are in the works, with Brii Biosciences recently announcing results of their Phase 2b ENRICH and ENHANCE trials. The trials tested the immunotherapy, BRII-179 in combination with the siRNA drug elebsiran discovered by Alnylam Pharmaceuticals and licensed by Vir Biotechnology, and the FDA-approved antiviral PEG-IFN alpha (pegylated interferon-alpha). The new results suggest that a priming strategy whereby BRII-179 is introduced before treatment with elebsiran and PEG-IFN alpha could result in a new functional cure approach for patients. “These initial [end-of-treatment] data provide important insights into the relative performance of the ENRICH and ENHANCE study designs,” said David Margolis, Chief Medical Officer of Brii Biosciences, in the press release. An uncertain future While the company noted that they will share the full dataset at a scientific conference later this year, they noted in the recent report that the priming strategy studied in the ENRICH trial achieved hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) loss rates of 42.9 percent with five doses every three weeks and 40 percent with seven doses every two weeks. The addition of the siRNA drug elebsiran specifically produced higher functional cure rates compared to PEG-IFN alpha alone (which achieved a 10.2 percent functional cure rate). news.title_zh: Brii Biosciences 距离乙型肝炎 功能性治愈 又近了一步,但未来仍不确定 - Drug Discovery News
news.source_body_en: Brii Biosciences has reported promising results from their Phase 2b ENRICH and ENHANCE trials for a functional cure of hepatitis B. The ENRICH trial, which tested the immunotherapy BRII-179 in combination with the siRNA drug elebsiran and the FDA-approved antiviral PEG-IFN alpha, achieved HBsAg loss rates of 42.9% with five doses every three weeks and 40% with seven doses every two weeks. In contrast, the ENHANCE trial, which involved concurrent administration of the three medications, showed a lower HBsAg loss rate of 25.5%. These findings suggest that the ENRICH study design may be more effective for a functional cure. However, the company emphasized that future Phase 3 trials are currently in limbo due to ongoing arbitration with Vir Biotechnology regarding the manufacturing of elebsiran. Despite the promising results, the data is still preliminary and requires further long-term follow-up to assess the durability of the HBsAg loss. The potential approval of GSK's bepirovirsen by Japan’s Ministry of Health, Labour, and Welfare could provide an alternative functional cure option, though no direct comparisons have been made between the two treatments due to differences in study designs and patient populations.
news.content_zh: Brii Biosciences 已报告其针对乙型肝炎的 功能性治愈 的 Phase 2b ENRICH 和 ENHANCE 试验取得了有希望的结果。ENRICH 试验测试了免疫疗法 BRII-179 与 siRNA 药物 elebsiran 以及 FDA 批准的 抗病毒药物 PEG-IFN α 联合使用,取得了 HBsAg 丢失率为 42.9%(每三周五剂)和 40%(每两周七剂)。相比之下,ENHANCE 试验在三种药物同步给药的情况下,HBsAg 丢失率为 25.5%,较低。这些发现提示 ENRICH 研究设计可能对 功能性治愈 更有效。然而,公司强调,由于与 Vir Biotechnology 就 elebsiran 生产的仲裁仍在进行,未来的 Phase 3 试验目前处于不确定状态。尽管结果令人鼓舞,数据仍属初步,需要进一步的长期随访以评估 HBsAg 丢失的持久性。日本厚生劳动省可能批准 GSK 的 bepirovirsen,这可能提供另一种 功能性治愈 选项,尽管由于研究设计和患者人群的差异,尚未对两种 治疗 进行直接比较。

Play Mute Current Time 0:00 / Duration 0:00 Loaded: 0% Stream Type LIVE Seek to live, currently playing liveLIVE Remaining Time -0:00 1x Playback Rate Picture-in-PictureFullscreen Episodes in this series Previous slideNext slide EP. 1 Understanding the Immune Pathophysiology Driving Chronic Hepatitis B EP. 2 Hepatitis B Epidemiology: Closing the Screening and Diagnosis Gap EP. 3 Monitoring Disease Progression and Liver Cancer Risk in Hepatitis B EP. 4 Quantitative HBsAg Testing and the Path to Finite-Duration Therapy EP. 5 Unmet Needs and Long-Term Antiviral Safety in Hepatitis B Care EP. 6 Why Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C Cures Are Fundamentally Different EP. 7 The Next Frontier in Hepatitis B Functional and Virologic Cure EP. 8 Rethinking Standard of Care and the Promise of Functional Cure Now Playing EP. 9 How Bepirovirsen Targets the Hepatitis B Viral Lifecycle EP. 10 Inside the Be-Well Trials: Design, Population, and Patient Selection This episode, "How Bepirovirsen Targets the Hepatitis B Viral Lifecycle," features the panel debating how much of this agent's effect is direct versus immunologic. Dr. Chung introduces the first pipeline agent for discussion, bepirovirsen, which recently reported phase 3 data, and asks Dr. Gish to walk through its mechanism of action. Dr. Gish notes this is a bit of a controversial topic, pointing to published correspondence and editorial debate on the subject. He first explains how the virus replicates and persists, describing a mini-chromosome intermediate called cccDNA that serves as a replication template from which messenger RNA is transcribed into viral proteins. He adds that the virus also integrates into the liver cell genome, where that integrated DNA mostly produces truncated surface antigen. One strategy toward functional cure targets cccDNA directly or targets the integrated DNA, while bepirovirsen, an antisense oligonucleotide, instead targets the RNA intermediate before it can be translated into protein, binding to it and triggering a cleavage step. Dr. Gish explains that early trials with this antisense oligonucleotide approach revealed unexpected flares and liver enzyme changes that were not well understood at the time. As development moved from a targeted formulation to an unconjugated, or naked, oligonucleotide, the ALT effect persisted, and researchers eventually attributed it to an immunologic event rather than a purely direct antiviral effect. He says the exact proportion of benefit from direct RNA binding and cleavage versus an inflammatory immune response remains unclear, placing himself in what he calls the "60-40 club," and asks Dr. Chung for his view. Dr. Chung responds that he sees more than a casual immunologic contribution, since this compound's effects differ meaningfully from RNA interference agents that accomplish similar protein knockdown without producing the same signal. He suggests that this additional innate immune triggering may be the secret ingredient this particular drug delivers. Our next episode, "Inside the Be-Well Trials: Design, Population, and Patient Selection," turns to the phase 3 data behind this emerging therapy. read Hepatitis C screening at King Fahad Hospital in Lamu. [Mercy Kahenda, Standard] He walked into the screening clinic simply wanting to know his health status. But after tests, 48-year-old seaman and fisherman received news he had not expected: He had tested positive for Hepatitis B. He was counselled and linked to care. Moments later, he walked out of the Lamu County Referral Hospital determined to face the diagnosis and manage his condition. “I am not shocked. This is a disease that can catch anyone,” he said. He suspects he contracted the virus through unprotected sex. He said seeing other people living with Hepatitis B while on medication had given him hope he, too, could live with the infection. “I am happy to know my status. Not knowing would risk infecting other people. Hepatitis B is not a death sentence. With medication adherence, I shall prevent the disease from advancing.” For Beatrice*, however, the diagnosis came as a shock. The healthcare worker at a hospital in Lamu went for screening after colleagues encouraged her to get tested. To her surprise, the results were positive. “I cannot tell how I acquired the virus.” She suspects her work may have exposed her to the infection. As a cleaner, some of her duties involve handling and washing garments contaminated with blood. “Though I am encouraged I shall be well, I am somehow stressed. Living with a disease is not easy,” she said. Despite the shock, Beatrice plans to enrol for care and treatment. . Keep Reading Health experts warn hepatitis B remains a silent epidemic in Kenya How stigma fuels Hepatitis B in endemic zones Hepatitis B: How a new initiative is saving newborns from infection How three deaths set a scientist on a lifelong mission to unravel Hepatitis B Her case is part of an emerging trend that has caught the attention of scientists. Preliminary findings from an ongoing mass screening exercise in Lamu suggest Hepatitis B may be more prevalent than previously thought, particularly among people who inject drugs. The screening is being conducted by the National Aids and STI Control Programme (Nascop) and Kenya Medical Research Institute. Lamu was selected because of its historically high Hepatitis C burden. At least three in every 10 people tested for Hepatitis C have been positive, representing a prevalence of 29 per cent. But the latest findings are surprising. Kemri medical research scientist Dr Missiani Ochwoto said researchers expected to find more active Hepatitis C infections among those who inject drugs due to risks associated with sharing needles. About 300 have been tested, with a majority of those testing positive found to have Hepatitis B. “People who inject drugs by sharing needles are being found to have no Hepatitis C, and instead are found to have Hepatitis B,” said Nascop Viral Hepatitis and STI lead Dr Khadija Hassan. The finding could signal a shift in the pattern of viral hepatitis in Lamu, although scientists caution the investigation is still at an early stage. Antibody tests showed some people had previously been exposed to Hepatitis C. But further viral-load and confirmatory tests found they were not currently carrying the virus. One possible explanation is the impact of harm-reduction interventions, including Medically Assisted Treatment such as methadone programmes for people who use drugs. Scientists are also investigating whether Hepatitis B could be spreading through other forms of contact, including STIs, contaminated equipment and mother-to-child transmission. “It could be that Hepatitis B is higher in this population because of contact transmission that was not detected previously,” said Ochwoto. Researchers are examining the demographics and risk factors of those testing positive to determine whether there are identifiable clusters. Hepatitis B and C mainly affect the liver and can remain silent for years. Chronic infections can eventually cause severe liver damage, cirrhosis and liver cancer. Nascop is urging people to know their status, practise safer sex and, among people who inject drugs, use sterile syringes and seek harm-reduction services.
