Given the burden of hepatitis B and the risk of progression to cirrhosis and liver cancer, experts propose establishing a multi-center study in Vietnam to evaluate the potential use of umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells to support the treatment of cirrhosis. Báo Đầu tư•09/09/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on Google Add Vietnam.vn on Google 0 Opening up research avenues for stem cell therapy to support the treatment of liver cirrhosis caused by hepatitis B. Vietnam has a high rate of hepatitis B virus infection, while the treatment and management of progressive liver damage remain challenging. Given this reality, a new research direction is being pursued by hepatology and stem cell specialists, aiming to evaluate the potential use of mesenchymal stem cells from umbilical cord tissue to support the treatment of cirrhosis caused by hepatitis B. The proposal was discussed at a research protocol development workshop on September 8th, with the participation of experts from various hospitals and research institutions. Instead of immediately implementing the study on patients, the current approach focuses on developing a sufficiently robust protocol to answer important questions about cell quality, potential beneficiaries, timing of intervention, dosage, and methods for evaluating effectiveness. Vietnam has a high rate of hepatitis B virus infection, while the treatment and management of progressive liver damage remain challenging. Professor Pham Manh Hung, former Deputy Minister of Health, stated that Vietnam has a hepatitis B virus infection rate of over 10% of the population. The disease can progress to chronic hepatitis, cirrhosis, or liver cancer, creating a prolonged treatment burden for patients and the healthcare system. One of the reasons scientists are interested in mesenchymal stem cells lies in the mechanism of liver damage in people with hepatitis B. Professor Pham Manh Hung explained that liver cell damage does not primarily stem from the virus directly destroying the cells, but is related to the immune system's response in trying to eliminate the virus present inside the liver cells. Mesenchymal stem cells have the potential to modulate the immune response and have been studied in a variety of diseases. Among the cell sources of interest, mesenchymal stem cells from umbilical cord tissue have an advantage in terms of supply, as they can be collected from umbilical cord tissue after birth and cultured to produce cell products for research. For cirrhosis caused by hepatitis B, scientists expect that the immunomodulatory capabilities of mesenchymal stem cells may contribute to limiting excessive inflammatory responses, thereby supporting improved liver function. Many studies worldwide have tested this type of cell in patients with cirrhosis and liver failure, including cases related to the hepatitis B virus. Initial results indicate that the cell transfusions are relatively safe, patients tolerate them well, and some indicators of liver function and inflammation may improve. However, the gap between these initial signs and a recognized treatment method remains quite significant. The available evidence is insufficient to make mesenchymal stem cells a standard treatment for cirrhosis caused by hepatitis B. The results need to be further validated through larger, randomized controlled trials with rigorous study designs and consistent evaluation criteria. This is also why Professor Pham Manh Hung believes that Vietnam needs to move towards multi-center research, initially implementing it at a few capable facilities and then gradually expanding it. A study conducted at multiple centers can facilitate the assessment of whether the results obtained are consistent across different patient groups and treatment conditions. He proposed a study on a group of patients with decompensated cirrhosis due to hepatitis B virus infection who had a Child-Pugh score between 7 and 12. This is a scale used to assess the degree of liver function impairment. The research team could further divide the patients into two levels, 7-9 points and 10-12 points, thereby evaluating whether the potential for benefit from stem cell therapy differs between disease stages. Determining the optimal time for intervention was also a key focus for Professor Nguyen Thanh Liem, Director of the Vinmec Institute of Stem Cell and Gene Technology Research. He suggested that research should concentrate on patients with decompensated cirrhosis who are not yet in an advanced stage, when liver function still has the potential for recovery. The issue of dosage also needs careful consideration. Professor Nguyen Thanh Liem suggested using an appropriate dose that can be repeated multiple times instead of choosing a high dose from the start. This approach needs to be considered in terms of effectiveness, cost, and the risk of complications during treatment. Equally important is the quality of the cell product itself used in the research. Associate Professor Pham Van Phuc, Director of the Stem Cell Institute, Vietnam National University Ho Chi Minh City, assessed that mesenchymal stem cells from the umbilical cord are a suitable source for this research direction, but the quality of cells may vary between facilities due to differences in the source of the umbilical cord and the culture process. Therefore, product standardization is considered a prerequisite for ensuring the reliability and comparability of research results. Cells used for research must be sourced from licensed tissue banks and adhere to stringent manufacturing standards such as GMP. Sudden blurred vision can be a warning sign of stroke. Having suffered from diabetes for about 10 years, 50-year-old Mr. Tri was accustomed to monitoring potential complications that could arise after living with the disease for so long. Therefore, when his left eye suddenly weakened, his first thought was that his vision was being affected by diabetes. Subsequent tests revealed the cause lay in his brain; he had suffered an ischemic stroke. You may also like Mr. Tri arrived at the hospital for a check-up without exhibiting the commonly known signs of stroke, such as weakness or paralysis of the limbs, facial asymmetry, or difficulty speaking. During the examination, Dr. Pham Thi Thanh Truc discovered that the sudden loss of vision in one eye could be related to brain damage, so the patient was prescribed an MRI scan to determine the cause. The 3 Tesla cranial MRI results revealed signal abnormalities in the right occipital lobe, consistent with a recent cerebral infarction. Further examination revealed Mr. Tri had complete left-sided hemianopia, causing him to be unable to see the space to his left. The occipital lobe, located at the back of the brain, is responsible for processing visual information. Damage to this area can cause strokes to manifest primarily as visual abnormalities rather than the usual motor symptoms. Patients may experience blurred vision or partial loss of vision, but can still walk, talk, and move their limbs relatively normally, giving the impression that the situation is not yet truly dangerous. This particular characteristic puts some cases at risk of being diagnosed late. For someone with long-standing diabetes like Mr. Tri, the likelihood of misdiagnosis is even greater because blurred vision often leads patients to think of eye complications related to blood sugar. Mr. Tri was admitted to the hospital four hours after the onset of symptoms. The neurological deficits had significantly impacted his visual function, mobility, daily activities, and work. After assessing the patient's condition, the doctors prescribed intravenous thrombolytic therapy to restore blood flow, limit further brain damage, and reduce the risk of lasting sequelae. The patient was simultaneously treated with anticoagulants, and blood pressure and blood sugar were controlled with subcutaneous insulin. After 5 days, vision improved significantly, and there was no longer any weakness or paralysis in the limbs. The NIHSS score dropped to 0, indicating the absence of neurological deficits on this scale, and the patient could return to normal activities. Mr. Tri's recovery demonstrates the value of early detection of abnormal signs, even when symptoms don't resemble the common perception of a stroke. If blurred vision continues to be viewed simply as a complication of diabetes and the patient delays seeking medical attention, the opportunity for early treatment may be significantly reduced. Dr. Pham Thi Thanh Truc noted that not all stroke cases present with facial asymmetry, difficulty speaking, or weakness/paralysis of the limbs. Damage to the occipital lobe may cause patients to experience only visual disturbances such as blurred vision or partial loss of visual field. These sudden changes in vision should therefore not be taken lightly, especially in individuals with pre-existing cardiovascular and metabolic risk factors. For people with diabetes, the problem also lies in the risk of long-term, accumulated blood vessel damage. Dr. Truc warned that the risk of recurrent stroke could still occur if Mr. Tri does not properly control his risk factors. Maintaining high HbA1c levels for an extended period can increase blood vessel damage, thereby increasing the risk of cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events. Diabetes also creates a situation where symptoms can easily be misinterpreted. Patients, already warned about the risk of eye damage, may quickly attribute blurred vision to a complication of the underlying disease. Meanwhile, if changes in vision occur suddenly, a broader assessment of the cause is needed, including potential damage to nerves and blood vessels in the brain. Not only people with diabetes, but also those with hypertension, dyslipidemia, obesity, atrial fibrillation, or a history of stroke need close monitoring of risk factors. Taking medication as prescribed, having regular check-ups, and undergoing necessary examinations helps detect abnormalities early, thereby reducing the likelihood of stroke or recurrence. Warning signs of ulcerative colitis require medical attention. Persistent rectal bleeding is not only associated with common anorectal diseases but can also be a symptom of ulcerative colitis, a chronic inflammatory bowel disease that can recur and cause complications if not properly detected and controlled. For two consecutive months, a 59-year-old woman in Tuyen Quang experienced loose stools with bright red blood, about 3-4 times a day, but without abdominal pain, fever, or nausea. Initially, she didn't think her condition was related to chronic inflammatory bowel disease. Previously, the patient had undergone a colonoscopy at a local medical facility and received treatment for about a month, but the symptoms did not improve. The rectal bleeding continued, prompting the patient to seek further examination at MEDLATEC General Hospital. A general physical examination revealed no significant abnormalities. A rectal examination showed a small amount of bright red blood on the glove. The patient was ordered to undergo necessary investigations to determine the cause. The colonoscopy results showed inflamed and congested rectal mucosa, blurred vascular network, and scattered petechiae on the mucosal surface. Given these abnormalities, the doctors performed multiple rectal mucosal biopsies for histopathological examination. The results showed active chronic colitis. Combining clinical symptoms, endoscopic images, and histopathology, the patient was diagnosed with mild, localized rectal ulcerative colitis and prescribed treatment. You may also like According to MSc. Dr. Luu Thi Minh Hue , from the MEDLATEC Gastroenterology Center, ulcerative colitis belongs to the group of chronic inflammatory bowel diseases, causing damage to the colon's mucous membrane, usually starting in the rectum and potentially spreading to the upper sections of the colon. The disease typically progresses in episodes, alternating between periods of activity and remission. Clinical manifestations vary depending on the location of the lesions and the degree of inflammation, with bloody stools being one of the most common symptoms. Patients may simultaneously experience a feeling of urgency to defecate, increased frequency of bowel movements, loose or watery stools, intermittent abdominal pain, and bloating. In more active stages of the disease, fever, fatigue, weight loss, anemia, or other systemic symptoms may appear. Some cases may also present with extra-gastrointestinal symptoms such as joint pain or swelling, skin and eye damage, and liver and biliary tract abnormalities. It's important to note that rectal bleeding is not a symptom specific to ulcerative colitis. Many other gastrointestinal conditions can present similarly, ranging from anorectal diseases to polyps, inflammatory lesions, infections, or colorectal cancer. This overlapping of symptoms makes diagnosis based solely on external manifestations prone to misdiagnosis. According to Dr. Hue, colonoscopy plays a crucial role in determining the extent of damage and the severity of the disease. Normal mucosa has a clear network of capillaries, but in people with ulcerative colitis, this vascular system may be reduced or absent, and the mucosa becomes congested, edematous, rough, and prone to bleeding. In cases of more pronounced damage, the mucosa may bleed even without stimulation or develop shallow ulcers. With chronic disease, endoscopy may reveal pseudopolyps, loss of mucosal folds, narrowing of the colon lumen, or mucosal bridges. Doctors recommend that people experiencing prolonged or recurring rectal bleeding, especially when accompanied by changes in bowel habits, diarrhea, tenesmus, abdominal pain, fatigue, or unexplained weight loss, should proactively seek consultation with a gastroenterologist. [Mercy Kahenda, Standard] Scientists are reporting a spike in Hepatitis B infections in Lamu County. The findings are against the predominant infection of Hepatitis C, which has been high nationally and is linked to drug injections. The finding has raised concern among scientists and health officials. Lamu is leading in Hepatitis C infections, with at least three out of 10 people being infected, representing a prevalence of 29 per cent. The preliminary findings were discovered during the ongoing mass screening of the general population and people who inject drugs by the National AIDS and STI Control Programme (NASCOP), with support from scientists at the Kenya Medical Research Institute (KEMRI). In an interview with The Standard, the scientist said the team expected to find more cases of Hepatitis C among people who inject drugs because of the risk associated with sharing needles and syringes. This means we are not seeing the virus in these people,” added the scientist. At least 300 samples have been tested, with the majority of individuals testing positive for Hepatitis B. NASCOP Viral Hepatitis and STI Lead Dr Khadija Hassan said the findings were particularly concerning because they differ from the pattern previously documented in Lamu. Lamu was selected for the screening because of its high burden of Hepatitis C. Stay informed. The findings, she said, could have implications for Kenya’s efforts to eliminate viral hepatitis. “Together with scientists, we are digging deeper to see why we have a shift in the Hepatitis disease trend and what could be the underlying reasons,” added Dr Hassan. The screening is still ongoing, with scientists analysing samples to establish the extent of the infections and possible risk factors. According to a NASCOP official, one possibility of the discovery could be that interventions targeting injection drug use could be reducing Hepatitis C transmission. Lamu has been implementing the Medically Assisted Treatment (MAT) programme, including methadone treatment, for people who use drugs. With the interventions, Hassan observed that the findings could mean Hepatitis C infections could be declining. Additionally, according to Kemri, the discovery could mean Hepatitis B is spreading through other forms of contact that had previously gone undetected. Hepatitis is spread through contaminated equipment like needles, sexual contact, mother-to-child transmission, and other bodily fluid exchange with an infected person. “It could be that Hepatitis B is higher in this population because of contact transmission that was not detected previously,” added Ochwoto. Another possibility, according to KEMRI transmission among people who inject drugs could be shifting from Hepatitis C to Hepatitis B. However, the scientists say it is too early to conclude. “We need to look at the distribution and demographics of the people testing positive, their risk factors and whether there are any clusters,” emphasised Ochwoto. Hassan said NASCOP would continue working with scientists to understand the emerging trend and guide the next response. “We are continuing with screening and testing so that we can understand the burden and the risk factors better,” she said. GxP News Home News Practice Events English Русский English News Новости фармотрасли R‐Pharm, Sechenov University win Russian grant to develop CRISPR‐based hepatitis B cure От GxP News - 10.09.2026 0 1 Telegram Email Print A project by Russian pharmaceutical company R‐Pharm and Sechenov University to build a manufacturing platform for treating chronic hepatitis B using CRISPR‐Cas9 genome‐editing technology has won a grant in the Russian Science Foundation competition in memory of academician Yevgeny Velikhov. The competition was held on the president’s instructions and was aimed at developing new bioeconomy technology solutions for pharmaceuticals and healthcare. The development involves creating a scalable platform for packaging CRISPR‐Cas9 complexes targeting the hepatitis B virus into membrane nanoparticles. This would enable systemic delivery of gene editors in vivo for complete viral elimination. CRISPR‐Cas9 is a targeted genome‐editing technology, also known as “molecular scissors”. It is based on the action of the Cas9 nuclease protein, which cuts DNA. The system directs Cas9 precisely to the genome site where changes need to be made. According to R‐Pharm representatives, up to 200 copies of the complex can be loaded into a single nanoparticle (compared with 20‐60 for analogues), improving efficacy. The drug will have reduced off‐target activity and increased specificity for infected liver cells. The therapy is designed as a single administration, which could reduce the cost of the treatment course. “Genome editing is today one of the most dynamic areas of global biotech. We are moving in this direction from scratch, closing the full cycle: we are developing our own CRISPR‐Cas9 construct and simultaneously building an industrially scalable system for delivering these particles into cells. There are only a handful of end‐to‐end projects of this level in the world, and in Russia this is the first experience of building a full‐cycle platform,” said Vladimir Andrianov, Director for Partner Relations at R‐Pharm. The Russian Science Foundation grant will fund the transition from laboratory development to a pilot industrial prototype. The company notes that the platform allows the basic construct to be retained when changing targets, with only the guide component being reconfigured – opening the way to personalised therapy protocols. In Russia, this is the first experience of creating a full‐cycle genome‐editing platform. Dr. Chung introduces the first pipeline agent for discussion, bepirovirsen, which recently reported phase 3 data, and asks Dr. Gish to walk through its mechanism of action. Dr. Gish notes this is a bit of a controversial topic, pointing to published correspondence and editorial debate on the subject. He first explains how the virus replicates and persists, describing a mini-chromosome intermediate called cccDNA that serves as a replication template from which messenger RNA is transcribed into viral proteins. He adds that the virus also integrates into the liver cell genome, where that integrated DNA mostly produces truncated surface antigen. One strategy toward functional cure targets cccDNA directly or targets the integrated DNA, while bepirovirsen, an antisense oligonucleotide, instead targets the RNA intermediate before it can be translated into protein, binding to it and triggering a cleavage step. Dr. Gish explains that early trials with this antisense oligonucleotide approach revealed unexpected flares and liver enzyme changes that were not well understood at the time. As development moved from a targeted formulation to an unconjugated, or naked, oligonucleotide, the ALT effect persisted, and researchers eventually attributed it to an immunologic event rather than a purely direct antiviral effect. He says the exact proportion of benefit from direct RNA binding and cleavage versus an inflammatory immune response remains unclear, placing himself in what he calls the "60-40 club," and asks Dr. Chung for his view. Dr. Chung responds that he sees more than a casual immunologic contribution, since this compound's effects differ meaningfully from RNA interference agents that accomplish similar protein knockdown without producing the same signal. He suggests that this additional innate immune triggering may be the secret ingredient this particular drug delivers. Our next episode, "Inside the Be-Well Trials: Design, Population, and Patient Selection," turns to the phase 3 data behind this emerging therapy. Noor Ul Ain Rehman Fri, September 4, 2026 at 7:50 PM CDT 4 min read GSK -1.05% GSK -1.05% GSK plc (NYSE:GSK) has reached two important regulatory milestones involving treatments for chronic hepatitis B and rectal cancer. Bepirovirsen, which is now branded as Hibsago, was approved by Japan, marking the drug's first authorization anywhere in the world. In a separate development, the FDA granted priority review to an application seeking approval of GSK's (NYSE:GSK) cancer therapy Jemperli for locally advanced rectal cancer. The two developments strengthen different parts of GSK's (NYSE:GSK) pipeline. Hibsago has secured its first regulatory approval, while Jemperli remains under FDA review for the proposed rectal-cancer indication. Is GSK plc (GSK) the Best Undervalued UK Stock to Buy Right Now? Bull Case The approval of Hibsago represents the more immediate milestone for the company, as GSK (NYSE:GSK) described it as the first and only treatment approved in Japan to deliver a functional cure for chronic hepatitis B. The approval was supported by late-stage studies in which nearly one in five patients achieved a functional cure. Although that result applied to a minority of participants, it offers the possibility of a finite treatment course for some patients instead of continued reliance on lifelong antiviral pills. Hibsago is designed to address chronic hepatitis B through three mechanisms. It blocks replication of viral DNA, reduces levels of hepatitis B surface antigen in the blood, and strengthens the immune response to support longer-lasting control of the disease. That multi-part approach underpins GSK's (NYSE:GSK) attempt to move treatment beyond continuous viral suppression. The commercial expectations are also substantial. GSK (NYSE:GSK) has forecast that bepirovirsen could generate more than £2 billion, or approximately $2.73 billion, in peak annual sales, and if the drug approaches that target, it could contribute meaningfully to the company's goal of producing more than £40 billion in annual revenue by 2031. In addition, the Jemperli development broadens the positive regulatory picture. The FDA has accepted the therapy for priority review as a possible treatment for locally advanced rectal cancer, and while a priority review shortens the agency's review timetable, it does not indicate that approval is assured. The FDA assigned an action date in February 2027, and GSK (NYSE:GSK) said the structure of the program could potentially allow a decision before that deadline. Jemperli had previously received both Breakthrough Therapy and Fast Track designations for the proposed use, demonstrating the regulator's willingness to facilitate its development and review. An approval would add locally advanced rectal cancer to Jemperli's existing authorizations in specific subtypes of endometrial cancer, expanding the medicine's potential patient population. Story Continues Bear Case Hibsago's late-stage results also reveal the treatment's principal limitation, which is that nearly one in five patients achieved a functional cure, meaning most study participants did not reach that outcome. Investors will need to see whether the clinical results translate into meaningful prescribing demand following launch. It is also significant to note that Japan is currently Hibsago's only approved market. Its first global authorization validates an important part of the program, but it does not guarantee approval or commercial success in other countries. GSK's (NYSE:GSK) projection of more than £2 billion in peak annual sales remains a company forecast rather than established revenue. The Jemperli development is earlier in the regulatory process, and while the priority review accelerates consideration of the application, it is not an approval. Jemperli is not currently approved anywhere for locally advanced rectal cancer, and priority review does not guarantee that the FDA will approve the application. The possible earlier decision should also be treated cautiously. February 2027 is the formal FDA action date, while any decision before then remains a possibility rather than a confirmed timeline. Conclusion Hibsago's first approval gives GSK (NYSE:GSK) a regulatory entry into functional-cure treatment for chronic hepatitis B in Japan, while Jemperli's priority review creates an opportunity to expand the cancer therapy into rectal cancer. Together, the developments provide tangible evidence of pipeline progress. The investment implications now depend on execution. GSK (NYSE:GSK) must translate Hibsago's Japanese approval into adoption and pursue access in additional markets, while Jemperli must still complete the FDA review process. These are meaningful regulatory advances, but their eventual value will be determined by factors such as approvals, demand, and commercial performance. Chimpanzees once used in hepatitis B vaccine experiments have undergone comprehensive health checks at a sanctuary in Liberia as part of long-term care aimed at giving the animals a chance to live out their lives in safety.The West African chimpanzees were examined at Humane World for Animals' Second Chance Chimpanzee Refuge in central Liberia, where veterinary teams carried out procedures including dental checks, X-rays, blood tests and nail trimming, sanctuary director Liliana Pacheco Ricote told The Associated Press.More than 400 chimpanzees were used by American researchers in hepatitis B vaccine experiments in Liberia from the 1970s until the early 2000s, Ricote said. Many had been captured from the wild as infants and subjected to invasive procedures during the research.Humane World for Animals said it assumed permanent responsibility in 2015 for the 60 chimpanzees that remained after the research programme ended. The animals now live mainly on a group of mangrove-covered islands at the sanctuary.The latest examinations were conducted under anaesthesia and were designed to provide a head-to-toe assessment of the chimpanzees' health, identify early signs of disease and help veterinarians develop individual care plans as the animals age, the organisation said. by Taboolaby Taboola Sponsored LinksSponsored Links Promoted LinksPromoted Links You May Like A Billionaire's Reading List: 5 Books Cuban Says Everyone Should KnowBlinkist Magazine Read More Undo The checks included examinations of the teeth, heart, lungs and nervous system, along with blood tests. The chimpanzees also received booster vaccinations and nail trims, with plans to examine the remaining animals."The health checks are a vital part of caring for these chimpanzees who have been through so much," said Belen Perez Hernando, the sanctuary's veterinarian.The chimpanzees are now typically between 30 and 35 years old. The full findings from the latest assessments are still being compiled, so the long-term effects of their time in research remain unclear.Ricote said the physical and behavioural effects of the experiments were nevertheless still apparent in some of the animals."They were used in very invasive research ... (and) went through a lot of experiments and pain," she said.Liberia has the second-largest population of chimpanzees in West Africa after Guinea. West African chimpanzees are classified as critically endangered as their numbers continue to decline.For the sanctuary, the health programme is part of an effort to provide the former research animals with specialised care for the rest of their lives."Seeing how much they hurt about what we've done, it gives me a lot of pleasure ... to give them this second chance to live with dignity the life that they deserve," Ricote said. supplementary_news.content: News World Chimpanzees used in hepatitis B vaccine research examined in Liberia UA.NEWS 05 September 2026 17:11 Comprehensive medical examinations have been conducted on chimpanzees at the Second Chance Chimpanzee Refuge in central Liberia that were previously used in laboratory research on a hepatitis B vaccine. This was reported by TimesLIVE , citing the refuge’s director, Liliana Pacheco Ricote. The animals had their teeth cleaned, underwent X-ray examinations and had their nails trimmed. The examinations under anesthesia included checks of the teeth, heart, lungs and nervous system, as well as blood tests. The chimpanzees are also receiving booster vaccinations. The refuge plans to examine other animals as well. Long-term care According to Humane World for Animals, the medical checks are needed to assess the animals’ long-term health, detect possible illnesses early and develop individual care plans as they age. The average age of these chimpanzees is between 30 and 35 years. More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram . In 2015, Humane World for Animals assumed permanent responsibility for 60 chimpanzees that remained after the research program ended. They now mostly live at the refuge on islands covered with mangrove forests. Research lasted for decades According to Ricote, U.S. researchers used more than 400 chimpanzees in Liberia for hepatitis B vaccine experiments from the 1970s until the early 2000s. Many of the animals were captured in the wild as infants. Western chimpanzees are classified as critically endangered because of a rapid population decline. Liberia ranks second in West Africa in the number of these primates, after Guinea. The results of the current medical assessments are still being processed, so the full impact of laboratory experiments on the animals’ health has not yet been determined. Learn more Build your reading streak0/3 today·Counts at 25% Veterinarians on the river islands near Marshall, Liberia, have begun sedating chimpanzees one by one for the most thorough medical examinations of their lives, decades after the animals were infected with hepatitis viruses in American vaccine experiments. The sanctuary staff describe the programme as a second chance for a colony that science used and then nearly lost. More than 400 chimpanzees were used by American researchers in Liberia between the 1970s and the mid-2000s, according to the Humane Society of the United States, which now cares for the surviving animals. The chimpanzees were injected with hepatitis B and other viruses to test vaccine safety and study infection, work that helped produce the hepatitis B vaccine now protecting billions of people worldwide. The comprehensive health checks, first reported by the Times of India, mark a turning point in a care arrangement that animal welfare groups fought for years to secure. From Research Colony to River Sanctuary The colony's history stretches back more than five decades. American scientists established the Liberian facility because West African chimpanzees were the only animal model that could be infected with human hepatitis viruses, making them indispensable for vaccine and drug research. Chimpanzees were the sole animal model for hepatitis B and hepatitis C for much of that period, and the hepatitis C virus itself was identified in the 1980s using chimpanzees injected with the then-mysterious pathogen, according to a review of the chimpanzee model published in viral hepatitis research. That contribution came at a heavy cost. A study tracking chimpanzees used in hepatitis C research found that HCV infection reduces the animals' lifespan, and scientists note that chimpanzees, unlike humans, can carry and continuously produce the virus while remaining essentially asymptomatic, complicating both research interpretation and long-term care. The research funding collapsed in the mid-2000s when the New York Blood Center, which had operated the Liberian studies, withdrew support for the animals' care. The chimpanzees were left on islands in the Farmington River with unreliable food and veterinary services, a situation widely reported by international media and condemned by welfare organisations. In 2015 the Humane Society of the United States assumed responsibility for the colony, funding daily feeding, island maintenance and veterinary care for the remaining animals, now numbering roughly 60. What the Health Checks Involve Sanctuary veterinarians anaesthetise each chimpanzee individually to conduct examinations that the animals never received during their research years, the sanctuary reports. The protocol includes: Blood panels screening liver function, infection status and general organ health Cardiac ultrasound to detect heart disease, a leading killer of captive chimpanzees Dental examinations and treatment, since many of the animals are elderly Parasite screening and deworming, a persistent threat in Liberia's tropical climate Tumour checks and body-condition assessment to guide individual care plans Several of the chimps are in their 30s and 40s, near the upper range of captive chimpanzee lifespans, so the exams are expected to shape end-of-life care decisions at the sanctuary. Results from each animal feed into a long-term medical database, giving researchers their first systematic picture of how decades-old hepatitis infections have aged this population. The Science They Gave the World The medical debt runs in the other direction as well. Robert Lanford, a hepatitis researcher affiliated with the Southwest National Primate Research Center in the United States, has written that entire generations are now immune to hepatitis A and hepatitis B because of vaccines developed using the chimpanzee model. The hepatitis B vaccine, rolled out globally from the 1980s, has driven sharp declines in liver cancer and infant transmission in high-burden countries, including across sub-Saharan Africa where the virus remains endemic. The research era itself ended by law and by listing. In 2015 the United States Fish and Wildlife Service classified captive chimpanzees as endangered, and the National Institutes of Health retired its remaining research chimpanzees, closing the door on the model that Liberia's colony had served. Institutions such as Texas Biomed have since identified alternative animal models for hepatitis research. Why It Matters Beyond Liberia For Liberians, the sanctuary is both a conservation asset and an employer, supporting veterinary staff, caretakers and boat crews in Margibi County in a country where formal veterinary capacity is thin. For the global research community, the programme tests a principle gaining ground in science policy: institutions that benefit from animal research carry a lifelong duty of care for the subjects. Similar retirement arrangements, including sanctuaries in the United States receiving NIH chimpanzees, are being watched by ethicists and by African wildlife authorities weighing how to absorb former research animals within their own conservation systems. Kenya's wildlife institutions and the Kenya Wildlife Service face parallel questions in managing long-lived captive animals, and the Liberian model offers a working template for veterinary monitoring of rescued populations. Sanctuary staff call the health checks a second chance, and for chimpanzees that spent decades serving human medicine, the phrase is more than a headline. The exams will continue across the colony in the coming months, with findings expected to guide both individual treatment and a scientific record that finally documents, rather than exploits, what these animals endured. 2026-09-08 感染前沿 感染前沿 发表于上海 HBVHIV 传染科新前沿 传染病医院 医生/ 主治医师 关注 互相关注 这项欧洲多中心横断面研究表明,在HIV/HBV共感染人群中,符合指南推荐的HCC监测对象比例非常高,但真正接受规范监测者明显不足。总体上,88%的患者符合监测适应证,而规范依从者仅占28%。 深度解析医学证据,DeepEvidence为你支撑决策 慢性乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)感染是HCC最重要的病因之一。即使患者已经接受核苷(酸)类似物治疗并实现HBV复制抑制,由于肝内cccDNA及整合HBV DNA仍可持续存在,HCC风险并不会完全消失。对于HIV/HBV共感染者,这一风险还可能叠加免疫功能异常、代谢共病、肝硬化以及HDV/HCV共感染等因素。 欧美指南均建议,对HBV相关肝硬化患者以及部分无肝硬化但属于高危分层者,进行每6个月一次的HCC监测,通常以肝脏超声为核心。但现实世界中,HCC监测依从性究竟如何,尤其是在已经纳入常规HIV门诊管理的HIV/HBV共感染人群中,相关证据仍然有限。 这篇发表于《Clinical Infectious Diseases》的Brief Report,正是围绕这一现实问题展开:在欧洲多中心HIV/HBV共感染者中,真正符合HCC监测指征的患者有多少?又有多少人能够按指南接受规范监测? 研究方法 研究设计:本研究为HDV-Europe Study中的嵌套亚组分析,采用多中心横断面设计。原研究于2024年6月至2025年3月在欧洲开展,纳入来自西班牙21家、德国21家和波兰7家中心的HIV/HBV共感染者。 纳入对象:年龄≥18岁,正在接受常规HIV医疗照护,且HBsAg阳性持续至少6个月。研究从病历中提取人口学、临床、病毒学、弹性成像和影像学信息。 HCC监测适用标准:依据2023年EACS指南,存在肝硬化者均应接受HCC监测;无肝硬化者如满足以下任意1项,也属于监测对象:年龄>45岁、亚洲或非洲血统、复制性HDV共感染,或白种人PAGE-B评分≥10分。 主要结局:是否依从指南接受HCC监测。作者将“病历中有记录已纳入HCC筛查项目,并每6个月进行一次肝脏超声”定义为指南依从。既往已有HCC者不纳入依从性分析。 研究结果 Table 1:研究对象基线人口学与临床特征 研究人群总体以中老年男性为主:本研究共纳入1308例HIV/HBV共感染者,中位年龄55.4岁(IQR 47.4–61.2),85.0%为男性。地区来源以欧洲为主(65.9%),约18%的患者来自撒哈拉以南非洲或亚洲。HIV传播途径中,男男性接触占48.1%,注射吸毒占16.1%。 HIV控制总体较好,但既往免疫损伤并不少见:30.0%的患者既往发生过AIDS定义性疾病,但入组时中位CD4+T细胞计数已恢复至624个/μL,87.0%的患者HIV RNA不可检测,提示大多数患者已获得较好的病毒学控制。 HBV复制抑制较充分,但肝病风险因素仍持续存在:抗HBV治疗方面,60.1%接受TAF方案,25.1%接受TDF方案,合计85%以上使用含替诺福韦治疗;83.0%的患者HBV DNA不可检测。然而,13.6%抗HDV阳性,4.2% HDV RNA阳性,20.6%抗HCV阳性,且10.5%存在肝硬化,说明即使在病毒控制较好的背景下,HCC相关危险因素仍然不少见。 Table 2:HCC监测指南依从性总体情况及分层结果 绝大多数患者实际上已经符合HCC监测指征:1308例患者中有14例既往已诊断HCC,因此被排除出监测依从性分析。余下1294例中,1142例(88%)符合EACS指南规定的HCC监测条件。值得注意的是,这1142例中只有123例(11%)是因肝硬化而纳入监测,而更多的是1019例(89%)无肝硬化但因年龄、种族、复制性HDV共感染或PAGE-B评分等高危因素而应接受监测。 总体指南依从性仅28%:在1142例符合监测指征的患者中,仅323例真正按指南接受每6个月一次的肝脏超声监测,依从率为28%(95%CI 26%–31%)。按国家划分,西班牙依从率为23%,德国36%,波兰31%,提示监测不足是多国共同存在的问题。 肝硬化患者的监测情况明显优于无肝硬化高危患者:123例肝硬化患者中,81例接受规范监测,依从率为66%(95%CI 57%–74%);而1019例无肝硬化但符合至少1项高危条件者中,仅242例接受规范监测,依从率仅24%(95%CI 21%–27%)。这一差异提示,临床实践中对“肝硬化需要HCC筛查”的识别相对充分,但对无肝硬化HBV感染者的风险分层和监测适应证识别明显不足。 不同国家之间还存在一定异质性:在肝硬化患者中,西班牙、德国和波兰的监测率分别为72%、48%和50%;在无肝硬化高危患者中,则分别为15%、35%和28%。但由于研究未系统收集医师、患者和卫生系统层面的影响因素,因此这些差异目前只能描述,尚不能直接解释其成因。 研究结论 这项欧洲多中心横断面研究表明,在HIV/HBV共感染人群中,符合指南推荐的HCC监测对象比例非常高,但真正接受规范监测者明显不足。总体上,88%的患者符合监测适应证,而规范依从者仅占28%。 监测缺口的核心并不只是“肝硬化患者筛得不够”,更重要的是大量无肝硬化但属于高危分层的患者没有被稳定识别并纳入半年一次的监测流程。因此,HCC监测需要更系统地整合进常规HIV/HBV长期管理中。 研究局限 首先,HCC监测依从性依据病历记录和各中心研究者报告判定,未进行外部核实,因此可能存在记录不全导致的低估或高估。其次,研究对象均来自已经稳定接受常规HIV医疗照护的人群,因此其结果未必能完全代表医疗接触较差或失访风险较高的人群。 此外,本研究以严格的“每6个月一次肝脏超声”作为指南依从标准,年度或不规律筛查未被计入,因此它评估的是“规范依从”而非“是否做过某种筛查”。同时,研究未系统收集医生专科背景、指南认知、提醒系统、影像资源可及性等变量,因此无法分析监测不足的决定因素。 思考 这篇研究的重点并不在于说明HIV/HBV共感染者存在HCC风险,而在于发现现有指南中的风险分层标准在临床实践中落实不足,尤其是无肝硬化高危患者更容易被遗漏。相比肝硬化这一明确的高危标志,年龄、族裔、HDV复制状态和PAGE-B评分等条件需要进一步综合判断,因此更难形成稳定的监测流程。研究提示,对HIV/HBV共感染者即使HBV DNA已得到抑制,仍应按照指南完成HCC风险分层,并将符合条件者持续纳入规范监测。 文献索引 Berenguer J, Ryan P, Lutz T, et al. Adherence to Hepatocellular Carcinoma Surveillance Guidelines Among People With Human Immunodeficiency Virus and Chronic Hepatitis B Virus Infection. Clinical Infectious Diseases. Published online June 1, 2026. doi:10.1093/cid/ciag341. PMID: 42219602. 阅读全文 你可能还想了解: HIV/HBV共感染者中,哪些因素会增加HCC风险? 在HIV/HBV共感染人群中,无肝硬化但符合高危分层的患者为何更容易被遗漏HCC监测? 慢性HBV感染产后女性接受Peg-IFNα治疗48周的HBsAg清除率和血清学转换率均为30.43%,且基线HBsAg< 1000 IU/mL的患者获益更佳。 【期刊导读】陈捷亮/袁正宏教授:干扰素α免疫调控机制全景解析 复旦大学上海医学院陈捷亮/袁正宏教授团队在Viruses上发表的相关综述重点阐述了PegIFNα在不同免疫细胞群中的作用机制以及未来联合抗病毒治疗策略的进展。 EASL2026 | 接受抗逆转录病毒治疗的HBV/HIV合并感染者加用聚乙二醇干扰素α-2b治疗48周的HBsAg清除率近40% 对于HIV/HBV合并感染者,在ART基础上加用PEG IFNα-2b具有促进HBsAg清除的潜力,且耐受性良好。 EASL 中国力量丨党双锁、贾晓黎教授团队在HBV所致肝癌新机制研究方面取得重要进展 该研究为深入理解HBV相关肝癌的发病机制提供了新的视角与依据。 EASL 中国力量 | 党双锁教授团队在HBV相关肝癌早期诊断领域取得重要进展 研究结果证实,该新型模型在诊断效能上显著优于现有的GALAD等7种经典模型,为我国这一乙肝高发地区的肝癌早期精准监测提供了强有力的全新工具。 【期刊导读】HBV感染不只伤肝,肝外恶性肿瘤风险显著增加 系统梳理了HBV相关肝外恶性肿瘤的疾病谱、证据强度及潜在致病机制,对优化慢乙肝患者的临床管理、加强肝外肿瘤的筛查与预防具有重要参考价值。 Chronic hepatitis can challenge that belief. The liver can sustain inflammation and damage for years without producing obvious symptoms. Dr Sandeep Satsangi, Lead Consultant – Hepatology and Transplant Hepatology at Manipal Hospital, Old Airport Road, explained that hepatitis is not one single disease. It describes inflammation of the liver, which can have several causes, including viral infections, fatty liver disease, alcohol, autoimmune conditions, medicines and inherited disorders. 2/7 Feeling normal does not always mean the liver is healthy Chronic hepatitis B and C can remain in the body for years. A person may continue working, exercising and following a normal routine while liver damage slowly develops in the background. WHO notes that many chronic hepatitis infections are asymptomatic. Its 2026 hepatitis B fact sheet says 240 million people were living with chronic hepatitis B globally in 2024, while only 27% knew their infection status. That gap explains why testing matters even when a person feels perfectly well. 3/7 The warning signs can be surprisingly easy to dismiss Symptoms may appear only after liver damage has progressed. Persistent tiredness, poor appetite, nausea, abdominal discomfort, dark urine or yellowing of the eyes and skin should not simply be brushed aside. Some people may also notice unexplained weight loss or swelling as liver disease becomes more advanced. These signs do not prove hepatitis, but they deserve medical evaluation. Hepatitis C can remain silent for decades before symptoms linked to serious liver damage appear, according to WHO. 4/7 Hepatitis is bigger than a viral infection “Contrary to popular belief of being a single disease, hepatitis is an umbrella term that refers to inflammation or swelling of the liver caused by several different conditions,” Dr Satsangi said. He explained that hepatitis A and E commonly cause acute illness, while hepatitis B and C are important causes of chronic infection. Fatty liver-related inflammation, excessive alcohol use, autoimmune hepatitis and inherited metabolic disorders can also injure the liver. The cause matters because treatment is not the same for every type. 5/7 Why testing can change the story Blood tests can identify hepatitis B and C before severe symptoms appear. For hepatitis B, laboratory testing is essential because symptoms alone cannot establish the diagnosis. WHO recommends testing people with suspected liver disease and several groups at increased risk. For hepatitis C, an antibody test is followed by an HCV RNA test when needed to confirm active infection. Modern antiviral medicines can cure more than 95% of people with hepatitis C. This is why waiting for jaundice or severe weakness is not a good testing strategy. 6/7 The liver often gives little warning “Ultimately, living with hepatitis begins with understanding its cause,” Dr Satsangi said. He added that some forms can resolve, while others need long-term monitoring and treatment. Hepatitis B can be controlled with antiviral treatment when indicated, while hepatitis C can usually be cured with modern medicines. The larger lesson is simple: feeling fine is not a liver test. When risk factors, medical history or symptoms raise concern, speaking with a doctor and getting appropriate testing can catch disease before irreversible damage develops. 7/7 Medical experts consulted This article includes expert inputs shared with TOI Health by: Dr Sandeep Satsangi, Lead Consultant – Hepatology and Transplant Hepatology at Manipal Hospital, Old Airport Road. Inputs were used to explain why chronic hepatitis can remain unnoticed despite the absence of obvious symptoms, and why timely testing and medical consultation are important. 2026-09-09 肝胆相照平台 肝胆相照平台 发表于上海 慢性乙型肝炎Rab7-STING轴 消化新前沿 企业/ 关注 互相关注 该研究整合患者肝组织、小鼠模型、细胞共培养及肝类器官等多层次证据,揭示了巨噬细胞Rab7-STING轴如何产生“抑制HBV复制却加速肝损伤”的双重效应。 深度解析医学证据,DeepEvidence为你支撑决策 慢性乙型肝炎(CHB)合并代谢相关脂肪性肝病(MASLD)在临床上十分常见。合并肝脂肪变的CHB患者往往具有更低的HBV DNA和乙型肝炎表面抗原(HBsAg)水平,但肝脏炎症、纤维化乃至不良结局并未同步改善。这提示,病毒学指标下降并不等同于肝病风险降低,代谢异常、脂毒性与先天免疫失衡可能共同推动疾病进展。 干扰素基因刺激因子(STING)是连接抗病毒免疫与炎症反应的重要枢纽。STING激活一方面可通过TBK1-IRF3-IFN-β通路抑制病毒复制,另一方面也可激活NF-κB和NLRP3炎症小体,加重组织损伤。HBV感染倾向于抑制STING,而MASLD相关的脂毒性与氧化应激则促进STING激活。在此背景下,CHB合并MASLD时STING的具体变化、细胞来源及致病机制尚不明确。 “脂肪肝学苑”第101期,特别推荐华中科技大学同济医学院附属同济医院王晓晶教授、宁琴教授及张斌豪教授团队发表于Gut的研究“Impairment of Rab7-dependent STING degradation hampers HBV replication but accelerates disease progression in chronic hepatitis B comorbid with MASLD”。该研究整合患者肝组织、小鼠模型、细胞共培养及肝类器官等多层次证据,揭示了巨噬细胞Rab7-STING轴如何产生“抑制HBV复制却加速肝损伤”的双重效应。 全文地址: https://doi.org/10.1136/gutjnl-2026-338065 01 材料和方法 1. 人肝组织样本:纳入对照组15例、MASLD组11例、CHB组15例及CHB合并MASLD组7例。通过Oil Red O、H&E、Sirius Red染色及免疫组化、免疫荧光和蛋白检测等方法,比较脂肪变、炎症、纤维化及STING信号变化。 2. 动物模型:采用HBV转基因小鼠和水动力注射pAAV/HBV1.2质粒的HBV模型,给予60%脂肪供能的高脂饮食构建CHB合并MASLD模型;设置对照、MASLD、CHB及共病组。 3. 遗传学验证:构建髓系细胞特异性STING敲除小鼠,明确巨噬细胞STING对HBV复制、代谢紊乱、肝脏炎症和纤维化的作用;同时构建肝细胞特异性STING敲入小鼠,验证肝细胞内STING积累是否足以诱导肝损伤。 4. 体外机制研究:将PMA诱导分化的THP-1巨噬细胞与HepG2、HepG2.2.15或HBV感染的HepG2-NTCP细胞进行Transwell共培养,给予棕榈酸刺激模拟脂毒性,并借助STING激动剂、抑制剂及自噬、内质网应激相关抑制剂解析信号通路。 02 研究结果 1. CHB合并MASLD呈现“病毒下降、肝损伤加重”的矛盾表型 患者肝组织中,MASLD及共病组均可见明显脂质沉积,其中共病组患者肝脏炎症及纤维化更为显著。在小鼠共病模型中,肝内HBcAg及血清HBV DNA、HBsAg均降低,而ALT、AST、炎症浸润及纤维化相关指标升高;同时,共病小鼠的葡萄糖耐量及胰岛素抵抗较单纯MASLD小鼠进一步恶化。 图1 2. STING异常蓄积主要源于巨噬细胞,并双向调控抗病毒与促炎反应 共病患者及小鼠肝脏中STING显著上调,并伴随TBK1-IRF3-IFN-β抗病毒信号及NF-κB-NLRP3促炎信号增强。免疫荧光显示,异常升高的STING主要与CD68或F4/80阳性巨噬细胞共定位,未见与CD3+T细胞明显共定位;进一步分离细胞发现,STING通路激活主要发生于巨噬细胞,而非肝细胞。髓系细胞特异性敲除STING后,共病小鼠HBV DNA和HBsAg回升,抗病毒作用减弱;但脂肪变、糖脂代谢紊乱、ALT/AST升高、炎症因子释放及肝纤维化均明显改善。可见,巨噬细胞STING是共病状态下“病毒被压低而肝病加重”的关键枢纽。 3. HBV与脂毒性协同抑制Rab7,阻断STING经两条溶酶体途径降解 HBV主要抑制Rab7转录,棕榈酸则促进Rab7蛋白的泛素-蛋白酶体途径降解,二者协同降低Rab7表达及其GTP酶活性。Rab7不足导致自噬体-溶酶体融合及晚期内体-溶酶体运输受阻,使STING无法被及时清除。 4. Rab7功能受损阻碍STING经两条溶酶体途径清除 研究显示,STING既可经自噬-溶酶体途径降解,亦可通过内体-溶酶体途径清除。在HBV与脂毒性共同刺激下,Rab7表达及功能下降,自噬体及晚期内体与溶酶体的融合受阻,溶酶体活性降低,最终导致STING清除障碍和异常蓄积。 5. 激活Rab7可同时改善病毒学指标和肝脏损伤 Rab7激动剂ML-098可促进STING降解,改善共病小鼠糖脂代谢、肝脏炎症和纤维化,同时进一步降低HBV DNA和HBsAg水平。上述结果提示,恢复Rab7功能并促进过量STING清除,可能有助于重新建立STING稳态,并兼顾抗病毒和抗炎双重效应。 图2 03 研究启示与思考 可借鉴之处:研究从患者肝组织中的异常现象出发,进一步追踪STING的主要细胞来源,并通过遗传学模型、细胞共培养和肝类器官等实验逐步解析其分子机制及细胞间传递过程,最后通过Rab7干预观察其对病毒复制、炎症和纤维化的影响。整个研究从临床现象出发,逐层深入到细胞和分子机制,并进一步开展干预验证,研究思路较为完整。 临床启示:对于CHB合并MASLD患者,HBV DNA或HBsAg降低不能简单等同于肝病风险同步下降。临床在关注病毒学指标的同时,亦应重视代谢异常及持续存在的肝脏炎症与纤维化风险。 机制启示:本研究进一步说明,STING在CHB合并MASLD中的作用并非单一。其抗病毒和促炎效应与发挥作用的细胞类型及STING在细胞内的积累状态密切相关。共病状态下,HBV与脂毒性共同抑制Rab7,使STING经溶酶体途径的清除受阻并持续蓄积。由此来看,影响疾病进展的关键不仅在于STING是否被激活,还在于激活后的STING能否被及时清除和终止信号。Rab7介导的STING稳态维持因此可能是连接病毒抑制与炎症损伤的重要环节。 局限性:本研究的人体样本量较小,现有结果尚不足以直接说明Rab7-STING轴与长期临床结局之间的关系。动物模型也难以完全模拟人类慢性HBV感染。另一方面,ML-098目前仍主要用于实验研究,其药理特征和临床应用价值尚需验证。此外,细胞外囊泡中的其他活性成分是否参与肝细胞损伤,本文尚未完全回答。 04 研究结论与未来研究方向 本研究揭示了CHB合并MASLD中”病毒复制受抑而肝病进展加速“的关键机制:HBV与脂毒性协同抑制巨噬细胞Rab7的表达和功能,阻断STING经自噬-溶酶体及内体-溶酶体途径降解;过量STING一方面通过TBK1-IRF3-IFN-β发挥抗病毒作用,另一方面通过NF-κB-NLRP3加剧巨噬细胞炎症反应,并经细胞外囊泡进入肝细胞,激活PERK-CHOP-NLRP3内质网应激通路,从而形成“HBV复制抑制、肝病进展加重”的免疫悖论。 目前这些发现主要来自有限的人体肝组织样本及动物和细胞模型。后续仍需在更大规模的CHB合并MASLD人群中验证Rab7-STING轴与肝脏炎症、纤维化及临床结局的关系。Rab7靶向调控的药理学特征、转化可行性,以及其与现有抗病毒治疗联合应用的价值,也有待进一步研究。 阅读全文 你可能还想了解: 巨噬细胞与肝细胞在CHB合并MASLD的STING信号传导中有何不同作用?
